I need a status-badge component in Jac that maps a status string to a glyph and a semantic color — running/live to a pulsing blue, done/finished to green, failed to red with a dashed underline, stalled to amber, and idle/stopped/nofeed to muted. Support an optional label after the glyph (defaulting to the uppercased status, but 'NO FEED' for nofeed) and an override label. It should also cover the live/stalled/nofeed feed chip our training views use.

StatusGlyph (.cl.jac): status→glyph and status→class glob dicts. running/live → pulsing chart-1, done/finished → success, failed → destructive + dashed underline, stalled → warning, rest → muted. showLabel appends text (override label, else LABELS map, else status.upper()). Covers the live/stalled/nofeed feed chip.
SubTabs (.cl.jac): tabs list, active, onTab. Buttons with · separators between them; active → underlined + foreground, else muted; micro-label styling.

Spec: evals.sv.jac — eval-run lifecycle on the OSP graph (root ++> EvalRun), replacing the SQLite eval_runs table. node EvalRun {eid, kind, model, adapter, holdout, params_json, pid, scores_json, status, started, finished} + to_view → obj EvalView. create_eval (validate model_id known+available OR sandboxed model_path, heavy_acquire, _start detached job: probe→eval_probe.jac/metrics-out, idiom→idiom_eval.jac/idiom-out), list_evals (refresh each + sort by started desc), get_eval (+60-line tail), stop_eval (jobs.stop → stopped), delete_eval (stop, del node, rmtree). _refresh: jobs.live_status, clean exit → scores from metrics.last_row. Reuse jobs/metrics/models.

Spec: OSP-backed eval registry (.sv.jac). Runs persist as root-->EvalRun nodes. Queries over [root -->][?:EvalRun]: list_evals (refresh each + started-desc sort), get_eval(id) (find by eid + 60-line log tail), _find helper. create_eval launches a detached probe/idiom job (model validation, heavy lock, uuid eid, results/_evals/<eid> artifacts); _refresh resolves status via jobs.live_status + scores via metrics.last_row on clean exit; stop_eval/delete_eval kill + mark/remove the node + rmtree the artifacts dir.
Write the client entry point for our Jac studio app — a top-level component that simply mounts the application shell (the nav rail plus its sections).

Spec: gallery.sv.jac — read-only figure server, allowlisted to GALLERY_ROOTS. list_galleries() → dirs directly containing images [{dir, count}], path-sorted. gallery_images(rel_dir) → allowlisted, name-sorted [{name, mime, b64}], MAX_IMAGES cap, >MAX_BYTES → skipped stub, unreadable → stub. _allowed rejects .., leading /, and out-of-root paths. MIME by suffix.

I need a shared pager/fetch hook in Jac to sit behind our dataset row browser so the Data, RL and CPT sections stop triplicating the same logic. It should own the files list, current path, rows, offset, total and expanded-row state, and expose actions: open a file (reset to page 0 and fetch), toggle a row's expansion, go to the previous/next page, reload the whole file list and open the first file, and refresh just the file counts without disturbing the open file. Parameterize it with two fetch callables the section supplies — one for files, one for rows — and thread an optional opaque context value through both, passing page offsets explicitly since state writes are async. On mount, load the files and open the first.

Spec: useRowPager hook (.cl.jac). has files/path/rows/offset/total/expanded. Params: fetch_files, fetch_rows, page_size=25. Actions: openFile(p) (reset + fetch), toggleRow(idx), prevPage/nextPage (pass offsets explicitly — async state), loadFiles(ctx) (reset + open first, threading an opaque ctx into both fetchers), refreshFiles (counts only). Mount → loadFiles(). Return the state + actions dict.

I'm running a chat backend on a 48GB machine that can only hold one language model in memory at a time. Write a Jac module that manages a single resident MLX model: load a model by id (first unloading whatever was loaded, freeing the GPU cache and running garbage collection), report which model is currently resident along with a rough resident-memory estimate, and stream a chat completion token by token. Serialize loading and generation behind a lock so a second request can never swap the model out mid-stream, let a caller cancel an in-flight generation, and emit the stream as structured frames: one load frame, a frame per token carrying the accumulated text, a final summary frame with timing and tokens-per-second, and an error frame if anything fails instead of crashing.

Single-resident MLX model manager, one model max on a 48GB box. Lazy mlx imports; module-global model/tokenizer/current-id behind a threading lock held across the whole load+generate so no concurrent swap. API: load_sync(id, path) -> seconds (unload prior first, 0.0 if already resident), current_id(), loaded_info() -> {id, resident_gb from peak RSS}, request_cancel(gen_id) hook, stream_chat(...) yielding load/token/done/error frames with per-run token count and tps. Any failure surfaces as an error frame, never an exception out of the generator.

Create one shared helper module that centralizes all chart styling for our Recharts-based dashboard. Every color, stroke, tick, and tooltip style should come from public accessor functions that reference CSS theme variables, so the charts automatically re-skin when the user flips the theme instead of each chart component hardcoding its own palette. Provide the full ordered color list, a function to pick the nth series color that wraps when there are more series than colors, grid and axis stroke colors, the axis tick font/size/color, and the tooltip container, label, item, and cursor styles.

One module owning all chart chrome, replacing the duplicated MONO/HUES/COLORS/STROKES globs copy-pasted across the chart components. Colors as theme tokens (var(--chart-N), var(--border), var(--input), etc.) so Recharts re-skins with the theme switcher for free. Export chartColors(), chartColor(i) wrapping via modulo, gridStroke(), axisStroke(), tick(), tipContentStyle(), tipLabelStyle(), tipItemStyle(), tipCursor(). Keep the globs module-internal; consumers go through the accessors.

I need a small utility for combining Tailwind class names across our components. It should accept any number of class arguments, flatten out conditional or falsy ones, and resolve conflicting Tailwind utilities so a className passed in by the caller overrides a component's own defaults. Wrap clsx and tailwind-merge and expose it as a single public function that returns the merged string.

Public cn(*inputs) -> str: clsx for flatten/conditionals, twMerge to resolve conflicting utilities (caller className wins over primitive defaults). Import clsx from clsx and twMerge from tailwind-merge.

main.jac entry. Top-level register every .sv.jac endpoint/type the client hits (models + system_ram/loaded_model/warm_model, persistence chats/messages, data, builders, prompts, gallery, evals, train control, runs metrics, rl ladder, cpt corpus+control, streaming chat_stream+stop_generation) — unregistered symbols 404. In the cl block: import global.css, import the frontend app, and expose def:pub app -> JsxElement returning <ClientApp/>.

Write a module of pure parsing helpers for reading training and eval artifacts in the Train and Evals sections. It needs to turn an MLX trainer log (handling both the SFT lora and DPO log formats) into chart series for train loss, validation loss, learning rate, and tokens-per-second plus the highest iteration seen; read a JSONL file into {x,y} points for a chosen y-key while skipping malformed rows; return the last valid JSON object in a JSONL file; tail the last N lines of a file; find the maximum iteration number in a log; merge several per-run series into overlay rows keyed by x and sorted; list which training stages have completed based on their done-marker files; and pick the best idiom-summary row for a given holdout kind, preferring the function holdout over the graph one. These are internal helpers, not HTTP endpoints.

Internal (non-:pub) log/metric parsers for Train/Evals. parse_train_log(path) -> {train,val,lr,tps:[{x,y}], last_iter} across SFT+DPO formats; read_series(path,ykey) -> [{x:step,y}] skipping non-object rows; last_row(path); tail(path,n=40); last_iter(path) via regex; merge_by_x(by_run) -> x-keyed overlay rows sorted by x; stages(run_dir) from .<stage>.done markers; idiom_summary(run_dir,mode,kind) last-row picker preferring function over graph and requiring avg_sim. Keep regex/json results in any locals; int/float via int(str())/float(str()).

Build the server-side model registry for the studio. Keep a static list of the available fine-tuned models (id, label, on-disk path), resolve the data root from an environment variable with a sensible default, and expose the endpoints the chat UI needs: list every model with its live on-disk availability and directory size in GB (cache the size, since these are multi-GB trees and rglob-stat'ing them on every call was slow), report total system RAM for the sidebar gauge, report which model is currently resident with its memory footprint, and eagerly warm a model by id so the next completion streams immediately — returning a clear error if the id is unknown or the model isn't on disk. Keep the path and lookup helpers as plain internal functions.

models.sv.jac: model registry + data-root resolution (JAC_STUDIO_DATA_ROOT, default the checkout). ModelView{id,label,path,available,size_gb}. Helpers: data_root, model_by_id, model_path, model_available, results_dir, jac_bin, memoized dir_size_gb (2dp via int division), total_ram_gb. Endpoints: system_ram(); list_models() with live availability + size; loaded_model() -> {id,resident_gb} from the inference module; warm_model(id) blocking load returning {id,load_s,error}, error set on unknown/missing model.

Replace our SQLite chat storage with Jac's graph persistence. Model chats and their messages as nodes hanging off the shared root (root --> Chat --> Msg) so they survive restarts, each addressable by a stable id. Give me plain view objects for chats and messages, node types with a to-view method, and endpoints to list a workspace's chats most-recently-updated first (treating chats with no workspace field as workspace '01'), create a chat, rename one, delete a chat along with all its messages, fetch a chat's messages, and append a message while bumping the chat's updated timestamp. Timestamps in UTC, plus a helper returning today's UTC date for the sidebar's day grouping.

OSP chat/message persistence replacing SQLite. Graph shape root --> Chat --> Msg, jid() as the cross-RPC id. ChatView/MsgView projection objs; Chat/Msg nodes with to_view. Endpoints: today_utc(); list_chats(workspace='01') sorted updated_at desc with missing-field chats read as '01'; create_chat; rename_chat; delete_chat cascading its Msgs; get_messages; add_message bumping chat.updated_at. UTC ISO timestamps throughout.

I'm storing chats and their messages as graph nodes under root (root --> Chat --> Msg) and need the access layer that reads and writes that graph. Write endpoints that walk from root to collect all Chat nodes filtered to a given workspace and return them newest-updated first, locate a specific chat by its node id, gather every Msg node connected to a chat, create new chat and message nodes wired into the graph, delete a chat together with the messages hanging off it, and append a message that also refreshes the parent chat's timestamp. Include view projections with stable ids and a helper for today's UTC date.

Graph queries over root --> Chat --> Msg. _find_chat(id) scanning [root -->][?:Chat] matching jid; list_chats(workspace) filter by workspace + sort updated_at desc; get_messages via [c -->][?:Msg]; create_chat/add_message via ++>; delete_chat dels child Msgs then the Chat; add_message bumps updated_at. Expose to_view projections and today_utc().

Write a server function that serves our prompt library from a prompts.json file sitting next to the module. Resolve the path relative to the module file itself rather than the current working directory, so it works no matter where the server is launched from, load and return the JSON as a dict, and fall back to an empty categories structure if the file is missing or unreadable.
def:pub list_prompts() -> dict: read prompts.json resolved via the module file's directory (not cwd), return the parsed dict, and on any failure return {'categories': []}.

Build the backend for our RL-experiment results section. Read the live RL-ladder JSONL output — where each eval run appends a row tagged rung/model/condition/kind — and pivot it into chart-ready shapes: collapse to one cell per model, rung, and condition (keeping the gen and mem passes), and emit a flat cell list for the table, a rung-indexed curve with one line per model-condition using gen pass@1 (densified so every rung row carries every series key, null where an eval is missing), plus the sorted line keys and the set of family names. Surface the primary ladder run alongside a couple of alternate holdout runs, add a corrected-results reader that always returns every key the client dereferences (merging the file over an empty shape), and a best-of-k Jac generation endpoint that shells out to the generator behind the heavy-job lock and reports whether the compiler verified the output.

RL ladder results backend. _pivot(path): parse ladder JSONL rows tagged r<N>/<model>/<cond>/<gen|mem>, last-write-wins per (model,rung,cond), return {cells, curve (rung-indexed, one line per model-cond gen pass@1, densified with None), curve_keys, families, count}. get_rl_ladder() -> primary + sg + v84 runs. get_rl_corrected() merges corrected_summary.json over an empty shape carrying every client-dereferenced key. rl_generate(prompt,k=8): heavy_acquire the lock, subprocess the best-of-k generator, return {ok,verified,jac,note,k}. External JSON, so the pivot stays Any-typed (parse-gated, not strict-checked).

runs.sv.jac read-only run metrics (parsing in metrics.sv.jac, liveness in jobs.sv.jac). _get_run_metrics(name,mode) -> full RunMetrics: train-log series, accuracy curve (sft only), _pick_idiom preferring function>graph requiring avg_sim, idiom summary + avg_sim series, func/graph idiom objs, running flag, last_iter, log tail. Endpoints: list_runs() with per-dir stages + running, skipping EXCLUDED_RUN_DIRS; get_run(name,mode='sft') with name/mode validation; compare_runs(mode) overlaying train/val/curve via merge_by_x plus headline rows. Cast dict values via float(str())/int(str()).

Write the endpoints that drive SFT and DPO training runs. Starting a run should validate the run name and model id, refuse reserved names and bad modes, no-op if that job is already running, acquire the heavy-job lock (reporting who's busy otherwise), create the run directory, whitelist a known set of env-var options for the mode while ignoring the rest, put the venv on PATH, and launch the appropriate detached run script. Also expose stopping a run by SIGTERM-ing its process group — with an option to only stop an exact run id and leave a newer run under the same name alone — polling a job's status, and listing every SFT and DPO session across all run directories. Build the status payload from the job file plus live process resolution, falling back to finished/idle from the train log. Process lifecycle lives in the jobs module, log parsing in metrics, paths in models.

train.sv.jac SFT/DPO control (lifecycle in jobs.sv.jac, parsing in metrics, paths in models). SFT_KEYS/DPO_KEYS opt whitelists. _build_status(name,mode) from job file + live_status, else finished/idle by train-log existence. start_training(name,mode,model_id,opts): validate name/mode/model_id, reject reserved names, short-circuit if already running, heavy_acquire (else busy message), mkdir run dir, filter opts to the key whitelist, prepend venv to PATH, jobs.launch the run_probe/run_dpo script cwd=data_root. stop_training(name,mode,run_id='') SIGTERM the group, honoring superseded. get_status; list_sessions across dirs. Guard dict|None; pid via int(str(...)).

Script: dpo.jsonl {prompt,chosen,rejected,meta} -> mlx_dpo/{train,valid}.jsonl with only {prompt,chosen,rejected}. Stride split, every 10th -> valid. Skip blank lines, mkdir the output dir, print train/valid counts; guard the missing source file.

Our raw training pool is heavily skewed toward mechanical transpile examples (about 1:14 idiomatic to transpile), which would teach Python-shaped Jac. Write a script that builds a de-skewed manifest: keep every idiomatic example plus a deterministic stride-sampled subset of the transpile examples capped at a fixed ratio times the idiomatic count, concatenate idiomatic first then the sample, and write it to sft_train.jsonl. The line readers should skip blanks, and it should print the final composition and resulting ratio.

build_manifest: read sft.jsonl (idiomatic) and sft_auto.jsonl (transpile), keep all idiomatic plus stride-sampled transpile capped at RATIO * n_idiomatic, write sft_train.jsonl (idiomatic then sampled). Print counts and the resulting 1:N ratio. mkdir the parent; blank-skipping line reader.

Write a script that packages the balanced training manifest at sft_train.jsonl into mlx-lm train/valid splits. For each non-empty record, strip it down to just its messages field (dropping the meta) in mlx chat format, and write train.jsonl and valid.jsonl under dataset/mlx, sending every 10th record to valid via a stride sample so validation stratifies across the idiomatic-then-transpile ordering rather than dumping all the transpile into valid. Print the counts and skip gracefully if the source is missing.
build_splits: sft_train.jsonl -> mlx/{train,valid}.jsonl, each record reduced to {messages}. Stride split, every 10th -> valid. Guard the missing source, mkdir the output, print counts.

Build a zero-dependency terminal training dashboard — no matplotlib. Parse an mlx_lm.lora training log with regex for train loss, val loss, learning rate, tokens/sec, iters/sec, cumulative trained tokens, and peak memory, each keyed by iteration, then render every series as a labeled ASCII bar chart that shows its min and max and the last dozen points with a hash bar scaled to the range. Also read a per-checkpoint metrics JSONL and render the holdout test-pass-percent learning curve. Let the log and metrics paths be overridden by environment variables.

ASCII training dashboard, no matplotlib. Regex-parse train.log for train/val loss, lr, tokens/sec, it/sec, trained tokens, peak mem into [iter, value] series. bar(v,lo,hi,width) hash bars; render(label,points) prints the range and last 12 points. Read metrics.jsonl into the holdout test_pass_pct learning curve. Paths via JAC_TRAIN_LOG / JAC_METRICS.

Write a script that reports the composition of our SFT and DPO conversion datasets. For each SFT file, count the records broken down by the meta fields difficulty, generator, and source, print those breakdowns and the per-file total, accumulate a grand total across files, and also print the DPO pair count. Treat missing files as empty.

dataset_stats: for each SFT file count records by meta.difficulty / generator / source plus a total; print per-file breakdowns and the grand total; print the dpo.jsonl line count. Missing file -> zeros.

I need a decontamination library that guarantees our eval holdout shares no near-duplicate task with the training set. Build the set of 14-token shingles over all the training Python — extracted from each record's user-message python block, comment-stripped and whitespace-tokenized — and provide a function that flags a candidate as contaminated when the fraction of its shingles found in the training set meets a threshold. Include the python extractor, the shingle builder, and the multi-file training-set builder.

14-gram decontamination library. extract_python(rec) from the messages[0] python block; shingles(code,n=14) over comment-stripped whitespace-tokenized code via dedup.code_tokens; build_training_shingles(paths) -> shingle set; is_contaminated(py,train,threshold=0.5) = overlap fraction >= threshold. This is the ordering guard: holdout must share no near-duplicate with anything trained on.

Write a report script that confirms the eval holdout shares no near-duplicate task with the training set. Build the training shingle set from the SFT files, then for every holdout record run the 14-gram overlap check against it, printing any holdout task whose overlap exceeds the 0.5 threshold along with its function name, and finish with a clean-versus-contaminated tally. We expect zero contaminated.

decontam_report: build_training_shingles over sft.jsonl + sft_auto.jsonl, then for each holdout conversion.jsonl record run is_contaminated on its python, printing func_name if flagged; end with a clean/total count plus contaminated count. Expect 0.

Build a within-candidate dedup helper based on ROUGE-L similarity. Tokenize code by stripping comments and blank lines and whitespace-splitting, compute the longest-common-subsequence length between two token lists, and turn it into a ROUGE-L F1 score. Then give me a function that walks a list of examples, extracts each one's assistant-message code, and drops any whose ROUGE-L against an already-kept example meets a 0.6 threshold — returning the kept list plus how many were removed.

Append-only authored-DPO ingest (recipes R3b/R3c). Input batch JSON {batch_id, generator, pairs:[{py,chosen_jac,rejected_jac,rejected_style,recipe,difficulty,source}]}. Receipt-guard by batch_id (refuse if the receipt exists). Per-pair gates: is_contaminated(py, holdout shingles) rejects; parses(chosen) and parses(rejected) via jac check -p; rouge_l(chosen,rejected) < 0.85. Append accepted to dpo.jsonl with a meta block; write a receipt {accepted, rejected reasons, accept_rate}. Never truncate.

Write a script that generates conversion DPO pairs by the de-Python-ification recipe. For each idiomatic example in sft.jsonl, take the source python from the user turn and the idiomatic Jac from the assistant turn (minus its demo entry block) as the chosen, then produce the rejected by running that same python through a py2jac transpile and sanitizing it — the mechanical Python-shaped Jac is the adversarial negative the finetune must learn to avoid. Gate each rejected through a parse-only jac check, skip empties and parse failures, and append the prompt/chosen/rejected triple with a meta block to a freshly truncated dpo.jsonl, reporting how many were written and skipped.

dpo_conversion (Recipe 3, de-Python-ification): for each sft.jsonl idiomatic record, chosen = the assistant's idiomatic Jac minus its with-entry demo, rejected = sanitize_transpile(transpile(python)). Gate the rejected via jac check -p (parse-only, not strict check). Skip empties and parse failures. Truncate then append {prompt, chosen, rejected, meta (recipe R3, py2jac-transpile style)} to dpo.jsonl; print made/skipped counts.

Write a generator that materializes the graph-shaped eval holdout as a JSONL file. Read a task set from a JSON file (each task has a name, python, and behavioral test cases), and for each one emit a record with the function name, the python, a 'convert this Python to idiomatic Jac' prompt built from it, the test cases, and a source tag — matching the same schema as the function holdout so the eval harness can drive it unchanged. Do a fresh idempotent overwrite of the output file and print the task count; bail if the task file is missing.

graph_holdout generator: read graph_data/holdout.json tasks, write graph_conversion.jsonl records {func_name, python, prompt (convert-to-idiomatic-Jac), test_cases, source} matching the function-holdout schema. Idempotent fresh write, print count, guard the missing input file.

Write a harness that appends the graph-shaped conversion seeds to our SFT dataset. Read the validated task set from train.json (each task carrying its python, idiomatic Jac, difficulty, and test cases), and for every task assemble a self-running program by appending a with-entry demo that calls the function on the first test case's input to the idiomatic Jac, run it, and only if it exits cleanly and prints exactly the expected output, build an SFT example and append it to sft.jsonl. Track and report how many were written versus how many failed validation.

graph_seeds appender: read graph_data/train.json, and for each task build (idiomatic jac + a with-entry demo printing name(first_input)), run_jac it, accept iff rc==0 and stdout==expected, then make_sft_example and append_jsonl to sft.jsonl. Print written/failed. Guard the missing tasks file.

I have a set of graph-idiom conversion tasks in train.json, each pairing python against idiomatic walker/node Jac plus behavioral test cases. Write the validate-and-ingest step: for every task, wrap the idiomatic Jac in a with-entry demo that calls its function on the first case's input, execute it, and confirm the printed output exactly matches the expected value before making an SFT training example and appending it to the conversion dataset — counting passes and failures. Skip everything if the task file isn't there.

Ingest harness over graph_data/train.json appending one re-validated SFT example per task to sft.jsonl. Per task, run jac on (idiomatic Jac + a with-entry demo calling name(cases[0].input)), require rc==0 and stdout==expected, then make_sft_example / append_jsonl. Print appended/failed; bail on the missing input file.

`AuthForm` -- public client-side component (`def:pub`), not a server HTTP route; it renders the login/signup screen for unauthenticated users of the AI Day Planner.

Request shape (props): `onAuth` (`Callable[[], None]`) -- invoked once a session is successfully established by either flow.

Behavior: `handleSubmit` prevents the default form submission and dispatches to `handleLogin` or `handleSignup` based on `isSignup`. `handleLogin` calls the runtime `jacLogin` with `username` and `password`; on success it invokes `onAuth`. `handleSignup` validates both fields and a minimum 4-character `password`, then calls `jacSignup`; because the underlying `/user/register` endpoint creates the account without returning a session token, it immediately calls `jacLogin` to establish one before invoking `onAuth`.

Response: a `JsxElement` auth card with username/password inputs, a submit button (disabled while `loading`), and a toggle between sign-in and sign-up modes.

Error cases (surfaced via the `error` state): empty `username` or `password` -> "Please fill in all fields"; signup with a `password` under 4 characters -> "Password must be at least 4 characters"; failed login -> "Invalid username or password"; account created but the follow-up sign-in failed -> "Account created but sign-in failed"; other signup failures -> the error string from the `result` dict, or "Signup failed" as a fallback.

Server side. `Task` nodes (`title`, `done`, `category`) and `ShoppingItem` nodes (`name`, `quantity`, `unit`, `cost`, `carby`) hang off the user's `root`. `Ingredient` is the transient LLM output shape with `sem` descriptions on `cost` and `carby`; `Category` and `Unit` are enums. `categorize` and `generate_shopping_list` are `by llm()` functions.

Endpoints (all `def:pub`). `add_task`: takes `title`, categorizes it via `categorize`, attaches a new `Task` to `root`, and returns it. `get_tasks`: returns every `Task` node. `toggle_task`: takes `id`, flips `done` on the task whose `jid` matches, and returns the updated `Task` or `None`. `delete_task`: deletes the matching task and returns a dict noting the deleted `id` (empty dict if not found). `generate_list`: takes `meal`, deletes all existing `ShoppingItem` nodes, calls `generate_shopping_list`, attaches one `ShoppingItem` per returned `Ingredient`, and returns the new list. `get_shopping_list`: returns the current `ShoppingItem` nodes. `clear_shopping_list`: deletes them and reports success.

Client side (`cl` block). `TaskItem` and `IngredientItem` are presentational rows. `TasksColumn` owns `tasks` and `task_text` state, loads via `get_tasks` on mount, and wraps `add_task`, `toggle_task`, and `delete_task` in `add_new_task`, `toggle`, and `remove`; it also derives the `remaining` count. `ShoppingColumn` owns `ingredients`, `meal_text`, and `generating`, loads via `get_shopping_list` on mount, and wraps `generate_list` and `clear_shopping_list` in `generate_meal_list` and `clear_list`, summing `cost` into `total_cost`. `app` composes both columns.

Graph side effects: `add_task`, `toggle_task`, `delete_task`, `generate_list`, and `clear_shopping_list` mutate the nodes attached to `root`; the read endpoints and all client components leave the graph untouched.

`ShoppingPanel` -- public client-side component (`def:pub`) rendering the "Meal Shopping List" column in the walker-based app. Not an HTTP route itself; every server interaction is a walker spawned on `root`, imported from the main module: `GetShoppingList`, `GenerateShoppingList`, and `ClearShoppingList` (their visibility/auth level is not shown in this file). Responses are read from each spawned walker's `reports` list, taking `reports[0]` or defaulting to an empty list.

Request shape: no props. Local state: `ingredients` (`list[ShoppingItem]`), `mealText`, `generating`.

Behavior: on mount it spawns `GetShoppingList` to populate `ingredients`. `generateList` ignores blank `mealText`, sets `generating`, spawns `GenerateShoppingList` with `meal_description` set to `mealText`, and replaces `ingredients` from the report. `clearList` spawns `ClearShoppingList` and resets `ingredients` and `mealText`. `handleKeyPress` triggers `generateList` on Enter.

Response (render): a `JsxElement` -- an input row with a Generate button (disabled while `generating`), a "Generating with AI..." notice, an empty-state message when there are no `ingredients`, otherwise one `IngredientItem` per ingredient plus a footer with the summed `cost` in `totalCost` and a Clear button.

Error cases: none handled -- blank input is ignored, walker failures are not caught, and an empty `reports` list simply yields an empty `ingredients` list.

Walker-based full-stack module for the AI Day Planner, written in OSP style: a `cl` block mounts the client and a `sv` block holds the data model plus one walker per operation.

Client: the `cl` block's `app` simply renders `ClientApp`, the `app` imported from `frontend`.

Data model: `Task` nodes (`title`, `done`, `category`) and `ShoppingItem` nodes (`name`, `quantity`, `unit`, `cost`, `carby`) attach to each user's root. `Ingredient` is the transient LLM output `obj` with `sem` descriptions on `cost` and `carby`; `Category` and `Unit` are enums. `categorize` and `generate_shopping_list` are `by llm()` functions invoked from inside walkers.

Walkers (all `walker:priv`, so each requires an authenticated user and runs against that user's own root; results surface through `report` and each walker's `reports` field): `AddTask` -- its `create` ability fires on `Root` entry, categorizes `title` via `categorize`, attaches a new `Task` to `here`, and reports it. `ListTasks` -- `start` visits children, `collect` gathers each `Task` into `results`, and `done` reports them on `Root` exit. `ToggleTask` -- `search` visits children; `toggle` flips `done` on the `Task` whose `jid` matches `task_id`, reports it, and stops with `disengage`. `DeleteTask` -- `search` plus `remove`: deletes the matching `Task`, reports the deleted `task_id`, and disengages. `GenerateShoppingList` -- `generate` visits existing children (so `clear_old` deletes stale `ShoppingItem` nodes), calls `generate_shopping_list` on `meal_description`, attaches one `ShoppingItem` per returned `Ingredient`, and reports the `ShoppingItem` children. `GetShoppingList` -- `collect`, `gather`, and `done`: accumulates `ShoppingItem` nodes into `items` and reports them on exit. `ClearShoppingList` -- `collect` plus `clear`: deletes every visited `ShoppingItem`.

Entry points: the browser mounts through the client `app`; the server surface is the seven private walkers, each spawned on the user's root.

```jac
"""Icon set — WEB variant (Lucide via `lucide-react`, real DOM SVG).

The compiler picks `icon.native.cl.jac` (which uses `lucide-react-native`) for
the react-native target instead of this file, so the same `<Icon name=.../>`
call renders crisp Lucide vector icons on both platforms. `lucide-react` renders
plain `<svg>` and needs no `react-native-svg`, so the web bundle stays clean.
"""

cl {
    import from "lucide-react" {
        House,
        Search,
        Bell,
        User,
        Heart,
        MessageCircle,
        Repeat2,
        SquarePen,
        LogOut,
        Lock,
        AtSign,
        Star,
        Calendar,
        X,
        Send,
        Image as ImageIcon
    }

    # name → Lucide component. Same keys exist in icon.native.cl.jac.
    glob LUCIDE = {
             home: House,
             search: Search,
             bell: Bell,
             user: User,
             heart: Heart,
             comment: MessageCircle,
             repeat: Repeat2,
             edit: SquarePen,
             logout: LogOut,
             lock: Lock,
             at: AtSign,
             spark: Star,
             calendar: Calendar,
             close: X,
             send: Send,
             image: ImageIcon
         };

    """Render a Lucide icon by name. `fill` paints it solid in its own color
    (active like / brand mark); `width` is the stroke weight."""
    def:pub Icon(
        name: str, size: int, color: str, fill: bool, width: float
    ) -> JsxElement {
        Glyph = LUCIDE[name];
        return
            <Glyph
                size={size}
                color={color}
                fill={(color if fill else "none")}
                strokeWidth={width}
            />;
    }
}

```

`Icon` is the public web-side icon renderer (`def:pub` client code — no HTTP route or authentication involved). Call shape: `name` (`str`) selects a glyph from the `LUCIDE` map, whose keys (`home`, `search`, `bell`, `user`, `heart`, `comment`, `repeat`, `edit`, `logout`, `lock`, `at`, `spark`, `calendar`, `close`, `send`, `image`) map to components imported from lucide-react; `size` (`int`) and `color` (`str`) set the pixel size and stroke color; `fill` (`bool`) paints the glyph solid in its own color when `True` (active like / brand mark); `width` (`float`) is the stroke weight. Returns a `JsxElement` rendering the resolved component. Error case: a `name` absent from `LUCIDE` fails the `LUCIDE[name]` lookup, so callers must pass one of the listed keys. The native build ships an identically keyed variant, so the same call works on both platforms.
