`Calculator` is a stateful accumulator `obj` holding its running total in the `result` field (a `float` defaulting to 0.0). `add` takes `x` and returns the updated total; `reset` clears `result` back to zero and returns `None`. Both methods are declared here and implemented separately; no graph state is touched.

Implementation bodies for the `Calculator` methods. `add` increments `self.result` by `x` and returns the new accumulated value, so repeated calls keep a running total. `reset` sets `result` back to 0.0 and returns nothing. Both mutate the object's own state only; no graph nodes or edges are affected.

`Greeting` is a public client-side component (declared with `def:pub` inside a `cl` block) that renders a personalized heading. It receives `props` as a `dict` and returns a `JsxElement` — an `<h1>` interpolating `props.name` into a hello message. Pure render: no state, no side effects.

`Counter` is a client component whose reactive state is the `has` field `count` (an `int` starting at 0). It returns a `JsxElement`: a single button displaying the current `count`, whose `onClick` handler is a lambda reassigning `count = count + 1`, which triggers a re-render. No props and no server interaction.

`Timer` — a client-side component, not an HTTP endpoint; it mounts in the browser. State: `seconds` (`int`, starts at 0). On mount (`can with entry`) it starts a `setInterval` that increments `seconds` every 1000 ms, keeping the handle in `intervalId`; the unmount hook (`can with exit`) calls `clearInterval` on that handle so the timer cannot leak. Returns a `JsxElement` paragraph displaying the elapsed seconds. No auth, request shape, or error cases apply.

`TaskList` renders the caller's tasks fetched from the server. The `get_tasks` walker is bound via `sv import`; on mount (`async can with entry`) it is spawned on `root()`, and when the returned `result.reports` is non-empty its first entry becomes the `tasks` state, triggering a re-render. The component returns a `JsxElement` list in which each task renders a list item keyed by `task.id` showing `task.title`. Side effects: one server round-trip per mount.

`handle_add` is an async client handler that creates a task server-side by spawning the imported `add_task` walker on `root()` with a `title` of "New task". If the call yields anything in `result.reports`, the first report is bound to `new_task` and appended to `tasks` by assigning a new list, re-rendering the UI with the created task. Side effects: one server round-trip that persists a task, plus the `tasks` state update. Returns `None`.

`get_tasks` — endpoint auto-generated from a `walker:pub` declaration; the `:pub` visibility means no authentication is required and every caller operates on the shared graph. Request: no parameters (the walker declares no `has` fields), so an empty JSON body suffices. Behavior: on `Root` entry, the `fetch` ability reports every `Task` node one hop out from the root (`[-->]` narrowed by `[?:Task]`). Response: the reports array contains that list of `Task` nodes. No explicit error paths — an empty graph simply yields an empty list.

`create_task` is a private (`walker:priv`) walker: it runs authenticated, against the calling user's own subgraph. It carries one `has` field, `title`. Its `create` ability fires on `Root` entry, connects a new `Task` node to the user's root with `++>` (populating the node's `title` from `self.title`), binds the result to `new_task`, and reports it back to the caller. Side effect: one `Task` node and one edge persisted under the caller's root.

Two server endpoints contrasting visibility. `get_status` is `def:pub`: callable without login and returning a `dict` with a fixed "ok" status — suitable as a health check. `get_user_data` is `def:priv`: it requires an authenticated caller, and because each logged-in user gets an isolated root graph, the same code automatically returns data scoped to the calling user. Neither function mutates anything; both return a `dict`.

`create_task` — public walker endpoint (`walker:pub`), callable without authentication. Request: a JSON body whose `title` string automatically populates the walker's `has` field. Behavior: on `Root` entry, the `create` ability attaches a new `Task` node to the entry root via `++>` and reports it. Response: the reported node is serialized into the reports array of the response body. A request that omits `title` fails walker construction before the ability runs; a successful call always creates exactly one node and one edge.

`get_my_tasks` is an authenticated (`walker:priv`) read-only walker. Its `fetch` ability fires on `Root` entry and reports the nodes one hop from the root (`[-->]`) narrowed by type with `[?:Task]`. Because private walkers execute against the calling user's own root, the result is automatically limited to that user's `Task` nodes — no explicit ownership check is needed. No graph mutation occurs.

`LoginPage` is the client login form. It keeps three `has` string fields — `username`, `password`, and `error` — as controlled-input state and obtains a navigation function from `useNavigate`. `handleLogin` awaits `jacLogin` with the entered credentials: on success it calls `navigate` to the home route, otherwise it sets `error`, which renders in red under the form. The two inputs write `username` and `password` back through `onChange` lambdas typed `ChangeEvent`. Depends on the auth helpers imported from `@jac/runtime`; the side effect is the session established by a successful login.

File-based route. Placing this module at `pages/about.jac` and exporting a `def:pub` function named `page` registers it as the client route `/about`. Request/auth: none — the router simply mounts the returned `JsxElement` (a static About heading) when the path is visited; no server call is made. Error cases do not apply: an unmatched path just never renders this component.

Dynamic route page: the file location `pages/users/[id].jac` turns the bracketed segment into a URL parameter. Inside `page`, `useParams` (imported from `@jac/runtime`) returns the route's parameters; `params.id` is read into `userId` and rendered in the heading, so visiting /users/42 shows "User 42". Read-only — no state fields, no server calls, no side effects.

A route layout component. `layout` wraps every child page of its route directory: it renders shared chrome (here a `<nav>` placeholder) plus an `Outlet` imported from `@jac/runtime` — the slot where the router mounts the active child route's component. Returns a `JsxElement`; purely presentational, with no state or side effects.

`greet` builds a greeting string: it takes `name` (a `str`) and returns an f-string saying hello to that name, with no side effects. The module's `with entry` block demonstrates usage — it calls `greet` with "World", stores the result in `message`, and prints it when the file is run directly.

`Person` is a plain `obj` with three `has` fields: required `name` (`str`) and `age` (`int`), plus `email` defaulting to the empty string. `greet` returns a self-introduction f-string built from `self.name` and `self.age`; `is_adult` returns `True` when `age` is at least 18. The `with entry` block constructs a `Person` and prints both results. Pure object state — no graph interaction.

Declaration-only `Calculator`: an `obj` accumulating into its `result` field (`float`, starting at 0.0). Five methods are declared without bodies — `add`, `subtract`, and `multiply` each take `x` and return the updated total; `reset` zeroes the state and returns `None`; `get_result` reads the current value. The bodies live in a companion implementation file, keeping this file a clean API surface.

Method bodies for `Calculator`, supplied as `impl` blocks. `add`, `subtract`, and `multiply` apply `+=`, `-=`, and `*=` respectively to `self.result` with the argument `x` and return the new total, so calls compose into a running computation. `reset` restores `self.result` to 0.0; `get_result` returns the current value unchanged. All effects are confined to the object's `result` field.

This module models a small road network and a traversal over it. `City` is a `node` type carrying `name` and `population`; `Road` is an `edge` type with a `distance` field, so the connections themselves hold data. `Explorer` is a `walker` that accumulates the names of cities it reaches in its `visited` list: its `visit_city` ability fires on each `City` entry, appends `here.name`, prints the stop, and continues outward with `visit [-->]`. The `with entry` block is the entry point: it creates three cities, attaches `nyc` under `root`, chains `nyc` to `chi` to `la` with `Road` edges carrying distances, and finally spawns `Explorer` at `root` so it walks the whole chain in order.

Builds a tiny social graph. `User` is a `node` with `username` and an optional `bio`; `Follows` and `Blocks` are `edge` types carrying `since` and `reason` respectively, so relationships are typed and attributed. The `with entry` block creates `alice`, `bob`, and `carol` and wires three `Follows` edges, each stamped with a `since` date, using the typed-connect operator; `Blocks` is declared but not yet used. Side effect: the nodes and edges exist after entry, though none are attached to `root` here.

Demonstrates LLM-delegated functions. A global `model` wraps byllm's `Model` configured with "openai/gpt-4o-mini". `summarize` maps `text` to a `str` but has no hand-written body — it is delegated to `model` via `by`, guided by a reason string requesting a 2-3 sentence summary. `classify_sentiment` returns the `Sentiment` enum (`POSITIVE`, `NEGATIVE`, or `NEUTRAL`), so the LLM must produce a structured value rather than free text. The `with entry` block calls `summarize` and prints the `result`. Side effects: each invocation performs an LLM API request; nothing touches the graph.

Test suite for the `Calculator` archetype imported from the `calculator` module. Three named `test` blocks exercise the accumulator independently, each constructing a fresh `Calculator`: "calculator addition" verifies `add` accumulates across calls via `get_result`; "calculator reset" confirms `reset` returns the total to 0.0 after an `add`; "calculator multiply" checks `multiply` applies to the accumulated value (5.0 then times 3.0 giving 15.0). Failures surface through the `assert` statements.

A reference sheet of Jac import forms. `import from` with a braced name list pulls specific symbols — shown for a Jac package (`MyClass` and `my_function` from `mypackage.module`) and for Python's standard library (`path` from `os`, `Path` from `pathlib`, typing helpers, `defaultdict` from `collections`). Whole-module imports (`import os;`, `import json;`) bind the module object itself. The final form is a relative import: `Helper` resolved from `.submodule` within the same package. Imports only bind names — nothing here runs application logic.

Defines two enum styles and a consumer. `Color` assigns explicit string values to `RED`, `GREEN`, and `BLUE`, so a member's `.value` yields "red" and friends; `Direction` (`NORTH`, `SOUTH`, `EAST`, `WEST`) relies on implicit values. `describe_color` takes a `Color` member `c` and returns an f-string embedding `c.value`. The `with entry` block prints the description of `Color.RED`. Pure functions of their inputs; no state or graph effects.

`describe_value` inspects the runtime type of its argument `x` (typed `object`) using a `match` statement: `int` values, `str` values, and `list` values each get a tailored description — lists report their size via `len` — and the wildcard case returns "Unknown type". Always returns a `str`; no side effects. The `with entry` block demonstrates all three concrete branches with an integer, a string, and a list.

`fetch_data` is an `async def` function simulating a network fetch: it awaits `asyncio.sleep` for 0.1 seconds, then returns a string embedding the given `url`. The `with entry` block drives it synchronously with `asyncio.run`, storing and printing the `result`. Demonstrates that Jac coroutines plug directly into Python's `asyncio` event loop; no persistent state is touched.

This module pairs plain Jac functions with LLM-delegated ones and uses `sem` strings as the prompt-facing documentation layer throughout. A global `llm` holds a byllm `Model` ("gpt-4o"). `Summary` is the structured output type — a `title` plus `bullets` — and its `sem` entries tell the model what each field should contain. `word_count` is an ordinary function counting whitespace-separated words, and it doubles as a tool. `summarize` has no body: it is delegated to `llm` via `by` and must return a `Summary`, giving structured extraction. `analyze` is the agentic variant: also delegated to `llm`, but handed `word_count` as a tool with a `max_react_iterations` cap, so the model may call the function while answering. The `with entry` block is the demo entry point: it summarizes a sentence, prints the `title`, and asks `analyze` a question that exercises the tool.

Client-side authentication helpers built on the `@jac/runtime` primitives. `try_login` awaits `jacLogin` with `email` and `password` and maps the outcome to a status string ("success", "invalid credentials", or "error" on exception); the `ok` flag is pre-declared before the `try` block. `try_signup` chains `jacSignup` — which returns a `dict` checked via its "success" key — with a follow-up `jacLogin` to establish the session, distinguishing signup failure from login-after-signup failure. `perform_logout` wraps the synchronous `jacLogout` (no await). `Dashboard` is the protected-page pattern: a `def:pub` component that checks `jacIsLoggedIn` at the top and returns a `Navigate` redirect to the login route when unauthenticated. Side effects: session state changes in the runtime's auth store.

`Counter` — a public client component (`def:pub`), not an HTTP endpoint; it mounts in the browser. State: `count` (`int`) and `label` (`str`) declared with `has`. The `async can with entry` mount effect runs once and initializes `count`. Interactions: `handle_click` (a `MouseEvent` handler) increments `count`; `handle_input` (a `ChangeEvent` handler) copies `e.target.value` into `label`, keeping the input controlled. Render: an input bound to `label`, a heading that switches between a click tally and a "Start clicking!" prompt, and a plus button wired to `handle_click`. Auth, request shape, and error cases do not apply.

`BookCard` is a presentational client component for one book row. Props: `bookId`, the display `title`, and `onDelete`, a `Callable` that receives the book's id. The internal `handle_delete` handler — bound to the button's `onClick` and receiving a `MouseEvent` — simply invokes `onDelete` with `bookId`, delegating the actual deletion to the parent. Returns a `JsxElement`; the component holds no state of its own.

`ItemList` renders a `list` of `Item` values as an unordered list. """The `jac ai` agent contract -- the request a pluggable agent receives.

`AgentRequest` is the stable interface between the `jac ai` command and
whatever implements the `run_ai_agent` hook: the built-in byLLM agent, or a
plugin that replaces it. It carries the resolved CLI flags plus a
`CodeIntelligence` handle, so the agent can navigate the project
semantically -- precise definitions, uses, and types -- rather than by text
search.

The contract is an object rather than a fixed parameter list so new fields
can be added without breaking existing agent plugins.
"""

import os;
import from jaclang.compiler.code_intel { CodeIntelligence }


"""Everything a `jac ai` agent needs to run one session."""
obj AgentRequest {
    has prompt: str = "",
        model: str = "",
        n_ctx: int = 0,
        safe: bool = False,
        # Compact output: suppress the live reasoning stream, per-step/tool
        # timings, and step detail, leaving just tool calls and the answer.
        quiet: bool = False,
        # Open the agent in a web UI (a bundled Jac fullstack app) instead of the
        # terminal REPL, with a live cytoscape visualizer of the phase walker.
        ui: bool = False,
        cwd: str = "",
        code_intel: CodeIntelligence | None = None;
}


"""Build an AgentRequest from the resolved `jac ai` flags.

Roots a `CodeIntelligence` at the current working directory; the agent's
semantic tools share this single handle, so the project is compiled once.
"""
def build_agent_request(
    prompt: str = "",
    model: str = "",
    n_ctx: int = 0,
    safe: bool = False,
    quiet: bool = False,
    ui: bool = False
) -> AgentRequest {
    cwd = os.getcwd();
    return AgentRequest(
        prompt=prompt,
        model=model,
        n_ctx=n_ctx,
        safe=safe,
        quiet=quiet,
        ui=ui,
        cwd=cwd,
        code_intel=CodeIntelligence(proj_dir=cwd, lazy=True)
        # Lazy: the agent's structural tools (`project_map`, walkers) load from
        # the cheap, cross-run-cached structural index, deferring the full
        # type-checked pipeline until the first symbol/diagnostic query actually
        # needs it -- so startup and project-map calls don't pay semantic cost.
    );
}

```

"""Core types for CLI command definitions.

This module provides the foundational types for declaring CLI commands
with structured metadata that enables auto-documentation and plugin extension.
"""

import from typing { Callable }

"""Kind of command-line argument."""
enum ArgKind {
    POSITIONAL = 1,  # jac run <filename>
    OPTION = 2,  # jac run --session foo
    FLAG = 3,  # jac run --verbose (bool, no value)
    MULTI = 4,  # jac check file1.jac file2.jac
    REMAINDER = 5,  # jac enter main args...
}

"""Priority levels for command registration."""
enum CommandPriority {
    CORE = 100,  # Built-in commands
    PLUGIN = 200,  # Plugin-provided commands
    USER = 300,  # User-defined commands (highest priority)
}

"""Definition of a command-line argument with full metadata.

Provides structured argument definitions that enable:
- Auto-generated help documentation
- Type-safe argument parsing
- Plugin argument extension
"""
obj Arg {
    has name: str,  # Parameter name
        kind: ArgKind = ArgKind.OPTION,  # Argument kind
        typ: any = str,  # Python type for conversion
        `default: any = None,  # Default value
        help: str = "",  # Help text for this argument
        short: str | None = None,  # Short flag, e.g., "-s" for "--session"
        choices: list[any] | None = None,  # Valid choices
        required: bool = False,  # Whether argument is required
        dest: str | None = None,  # Override destination variable name
        metavar: str | None = None,  # Display name in help
        source: str = "jaclang";  # Source plugin that added this arg

    static def create(
        name: str,
        kind: ArgKind = ArgKind.OPTION,
        typ: any = str,
        `default: any = None,
        help: str = "",
        short: str | None = None,
        choices: list[any] | None = None,
        required: bool = False,
        metavar: str | None = None
    ) -> Arg;
}

"""Complete specification for a CLI command.

Contains all metadata needed to:
- Generate help documentation
- Build argparse configuration
- Execute the command with hooks
"""
obj CommandSpec {
    has name: str,  # Command name
        help: str,  # One-line description
        description: str = "",  # Detailed description (multi-line)
        args: list[Arg] = [],  # Base arguments
        examples: list[tuple[str, str]] = [],  # (command, description) pairs
        group: str = "general",  # Command group for help menu
        priority: CommandPriority = CommandPriority.CORE,
        source: str = "jaclang",  # Source package/plugin
        handler: Callable | None = None,  # Implementation function
        # Plugin extensions (populated at runtime)
        extra_args: list[Arg] = [],  # Arguments added by plugins
        pre_hooks: list[tuple[Callable, str]] = [],  # (hook, source) pairs
        post_hooks: list[tuple[Callable, str]] = [];  # (hook, source) pairs

    def get_all_args -> list[Arg];
    def add_extension_arg(arg: Arg, source: str) -> None;
    def add_pre_hook(hook: Callable, source: str) -> None;
    def add_post_hook(hook: Callable, source: str) -> None;
}

"""Hook context passed to pre/post hooks.

    commands: list[dict[str, any]], executable: str = "jac", shell: str = "bash"
) -> str;

def _static_bash(commands: list[dict[str, any]], exe: str) -> str;

def _static_zsh(commands: list[dict[str, any]], exe: str) -> str;

def _static_fish(commands: list[dict[str, any]], exe: str) -> str;

glob _BASH_TEMPLATE = (
         '_%s_complete() {\n'
         '    local cur prev cmd\n'
         '    COMPREPLY=()\n'
         '    cur="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}"\n'
         '    prev="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD-1]}"\n'
         '    cmd="${COMP_WORDS[1]}"\n'
         '\n'
         '    if [[ $COMP_CWORD -eq 1 ]]; then\n'
         '        COMPREPLY=($(compgen -W "%s" -- "$cur"))\n'
         '        return\n'
         '    fi\n'
         '\n'
         '%s'
         '    case "$cmd" in\n'
         '%s\n'
         '    esac\n'
         '}\n'
         'complete -o default -o bashdefault'
         ' -F _%s_complete %s\n'

         '    # Complete option values\n'
         '    case "$cmd" in\n'
         '%s\n'
         '    esac\n'
         '\n'
     ),
     _BASH_VALUE_CASE = (
         '        %s)\n'
         '            case "$prev" in\n'
         '%s\n'
         '            esac\n'
         '            ;;'

         '        %s)\n'
         '            case "$cur" in\n'
         '                -*) COMPREPLY=($(compgen'
         ' -W "%s" -- "$cur")) ;;\n'
         '            esac\n'
         '            ;;'

         '        %s)\n'

Takes raw object code bytes from llvmlite's emit_object() (a relocatable
COFF object for a `*-pc-windows-*` triple) and produces a runnable PE32+
executable using only Python's struct module. No external linker
(link.exe, lld-link, ld) required.

Mirrors the structure of the ELF and Mach-O linkers: parse the relocatable
object, lay out loadable segments at a fixed ImageBase (no ASLR / .reloc),
build the PE import directory so DLL imports resolve at load, apply
relocations, and inject the entry point.

Architecture support: x86_64 (dynamic-link against msvcrt.dll by default).
"""

"""Parsed COFF section."""
obj CoffSection {
    has name: str,
        characteristics: int,
        data: bytes,
        vsize: int;
}

"""Parsed COFF relocation (REL-style: implicit addend lives in the field)."""
obj CoffReloc {
    has offset: int,
        sym_idx: int,
        rtype: int,
        target_sec: int;
}

"""Parsed COFF symbol.

`weak_tag` is the symbol-table index of the default symbol for a weak
external (-1 when not weak); after parsing, a weak external's `sec_num`
and `value` are copied from its default so it resolves like a normal
defined symbol rather than being mistaken for a DLL import.
"""
obj CoffSymbol {
    has name: str,
        value: int,
        sec_num: int,
        storage_class: int,
        weak_tag: int = -1;
}

executable. Architecture is auto-detected from the object's Machine field.

    has obj_data: bytes,
        # Indexed by raw COFF symbol index; auxiliary records are None so
        # relocation symbol indices line up with this list.
        symbols: list[CoffSymbol | None],
        sections: list[CoffSection],
        relocations: list[CoffReloc],

        needed_libs: list[str],

        # "InitWindow" -> "raylib.dll". Drives per-DLL import descriptor
        # grouping; symbols absent from the map bind to the default DLL.

        # the `:pub` symbols, a .reloc base-relocation table (so the loader may
        # rebase it), and a DllMain that runs the init functions on attach.
        shared: bool = False,
        export_symbols: list[str] = [],
        init_funcs: list[str] = [],
        soname: str = "";

    static def link(
        obj_bytes: bytes,
        output_path: str,
        needed_libs: list[str] = ["msvcrt.dll"],
        symbol_lib_map: dict[str, str] = {},
        shared: bool = False,

Checks cover addition, subtraction, multiplication, exact division, power (i squared equals -1, using a complex exponent for type tracking), `conjugate`, equality and inequality in both matching and differing cases, and unary negation, with the flags returned in a `dict` keyed "add_ok" through "pos_ok". Unary plus (`pos_ok`) is exercised only on the Python and native variants: the client type evaluator loses the complex type after unary plus, which would make the following comparison use JS identity instead of the runtime's complex equality. The native variant also omits the power check. Pure computation with no side effects.

Cross-backend equivalence fixture for the os and os.path surface. `os_py` and the native-block `os_na` execute the same probes and return matching dicts: process-stable values compared directly (`os.getcwd` and `os.getenv` for "PATH", since both backends run in one process), the non-deterministic `os.getpid` checked only for positivity, exact-string checks over `os.path.join` (two and three components, trailing-slash and absolute-second-argument cases), `os.path.basename` and `os.path.dirname` with and without slashes, and existence probes via `os.path.exists`, `os.path.isdir`, and `os.path.isfile`. The one mutating sequence — `os.mkdir` followed by `os.path.isdir`, `os.rmdir`, and a final `os.path.exists` check folded into the `made_ok` flag — uses a backend-distinct temp directory path `p` so the two backends never collide on the filesystem. `os_cl` returns an empty `dict`, opting the ECMAScript backend out. Side effects are limited to the transient temp directory created and removed within each call.

Cross-backend equivalence fixture pinning MT19937 seed-to-sequence parity: the native implementation must reproduce CPython's random stream bit-for-bit. `random_py` and the native-block `random_na` run the identical ordered draw sequence — `random.seed` with 42, three `random.random` floats (`r1`, `r2`, `r3`), `random.getrandbits` at widths 32, 16, and 40, three `random.randint` draws over positive and signed ranges, one `random.randrange`, one `random.uniform`, then a reseed with 12345 followed by a final `random.random` (`s2`) to confirm reseeding resets the stream — and return every draw in a `dict`. Order matters: any divergence in the generator state shifts all subsequent values, so the fixture is sensitive to both the seeding algorithm and each derived-draw implementation. Integers must match exactly and floats within ULP. `random_cl` returns an empty `dict`; the ECMAScript backend opts out. No side effects beyond the module-global generator state within the call.

Cross-backend equivalence fixture for the deterministic, value-stable sys members. `sys_py` and the native-block `sys_na` both return `sys.maxsize`, `sys.byteorder`, and `sys.platform`, plus a `maxsize_is_i64max` flag asserting that `sys.maxsize` equals the signed 64-bit maximum. The harness compares the dicts by value, which is sound because both backends run in the same process on the same platform. sys argv is deliberately excluded here — it is non-deterministic under the JIT harness and covered by a separate nacompile test. `sys_cl` returns an empty `dict`, opting the ECMAScript backend out. Pure reads with no side effects and no parameters.

Cross-backend equivalence fixture for the tuple emitter. `tuple_py` and its client twin `tuple_cl` exercise the full surface: concatenation of a two-element tuple with a one-element tuple, membership via in and not in, the `count` and `index` methods on a tuple with duplicates, repetition with the * operator, and the six lexicographic comparisons over equal, differing, and shorter tuples (including the shorter-is-less case). Results are flattened to lists and bools and returned in a `dict` keyed "tuple_concat" through "lt_shorter". The native-block variant `tuple_na` runs the shared subset it supports — membership, `count`, `index`, and the comparisons on explicitly typed tuples — omitting concatenation, repetition, and the shorter-length comparison; the harness compares only intersecting keys. All three take no parameters, return the `dict`, and have no side effects.

Cross-backend fixture guarding shared module-level type declarations. The `obj` type `Pt` — two `int` fields `x` and `y` — is declared exactly once at module level, then consumed without redeclaration by all three backend entry functions: `shared_py`, the client-block `shared_cl`, and the native-block `shared_na`. Each constructs a `Pt` with values 3 and 4 and returns the field sum (7) in a `dict`, so any backend that failed to materialize the shared type or resolved the fields differently would diverge. This pins the rule that module-level archetype declarations are shared across every codespace, with each backend's codegen compiling the shared types its own code references. Pure construction and arithmetic; no side effects.

Declarations for enum type-checking utilities, mirroring Pyright's enum analysis. The module-level `ENUM_RESERVED_NAMES` set lists names excluded from enum membership (reserved attributes and sunder/dunder control names). `is_excluded_enum_member_name` returns whether a candidate `name` is reserved. `create_enum_member_info` extracts an `EnumMemberInfo` (or `None` for invalid members) from an `assignment` statement using the given `evaluator`. `validate_enum_member_annotation` checks an explicit per-member type annotation against the member's actual value type — necessary because the declaration site's symbol type is the enum-member wrapper, so the generic assignment compatibility check cannot see the mismatch; it reports through the `evaluator` and returns `None`. `build_enum_members` walks an `enum_node` (a `uni.Enum` or class-based `uni.Archetype`) and produces the full member map keyed by name, optionally validating each member against a required `enum_value_type`. `get_special_enum_value_type_from_bases` inspects `base_classes` using the `prefetch` type cache to derive the value type implied by special enum bases (IntEnum-like or StrEnum-like), returning `None` when no pattern matches. All functions are pure analyses over the AST and type objects; only the validators emit diagnostics as a side effect.

Implementations of the enum type-checking utilities. `is_excluded_enum_member_name` rejects dunder names and anything in `ENUM_RESERVED_NAMES`. `create_enum_member_info` validates that an `assignment` has a usable name target and a non-reserved name, then extracts the member's value type and literal: integer literals map to the prefetched `int_class` with their `lit_value`, string literals to `str_class`, and complex expressions fall back to `get_type_of_expression` on the `evaluator`; it returns a populated `EnumMemberInfo` or `None`. `validate_enum_member_annotation` compares an explicit annotation's resolved class against the member's `value_type` and emits diagnostic `E1001` on mismatch. `build_enum_members` is the driver: it collects member declarations from the `enum_node`'s `names_in_scope` (skipping reserved names and abilities so methods are never treated as members), handles assignments with explicit values, auto-increments `auto_value` for valueless members (continuing from the last explicit int, so a jump to 10 makes the next member 11), validates each member against an optional required `enum_value_type` plus its own annotation, and returns the name-keyed member map. `get_special_enum_value_type_from_bases` unions the MROs of all `base_classes` and uses prefetched type identity to detect the special patterns: an Enum ancestor combined with a str ancestor yields `str_class`, with an int ancestor yields `int_class`, otherwise `None`. Side effects are limited to diagnostics emitted via `emit_diag`.

Detection: `is_property_decorator_type` returns whether `decorator_type` is a `ClassType` for the builtin property class (via `is_builtin`), and `is_cached_property_decorator_type` matches a class whose `class_name` is "cached_property" and which originates from a stdlib stub (`is_from_stdlib_stub`). Checking: `is_property` returns whether `ty` is a `ClassType` instance flagged as a property class. All functions are pure constructors and predicates over type objects — no diagnostics, no mutation of inputs.

Detection predicates `is_property_decorator_type` and `is_cached_property_decorator_type` classify a `decorator_type` (`TypeBase`) as the property builtin or as cached_property from functools, returning `bool`. On the creation side, `create_property` wraps a getter `fget` (`FunctionType`) into a property `ClassType`, optionally bound to the enclosing `class_type`; `clone_property_with_setter` and `clone_property_with_deleter` produce a copy of an existing property `prop` augmented with a setter `fset` or deleter `fdel`, so the accessor triple accumulates across decorator applications without mutating the original. Finally `is_property` tests whether an arbitrary type `ty` is a property class instance. Declarations only — bodies live in the companion impl file; none of these touch the graph.

File-discovery utilities backing Jac module caching, JIR cache invalidation, and the formatter. `discover_annex_files` finds annex files (default `suffix` of `.impl.jac`, also `.test.jac`) for a `source_path`, searching the source's own directory, a module-specific folder, and the shared folder; it is variant-aware — a variant-suffixed annex must match the source's variant (`src_variant`) exactly, while a bare annex matches any source unless a bare head file exists to claim it (`bare_head_exists`). `discover_style_annex` locates the scoped-style `.style.css` annex paired with a module by shared base name, stripping any variant suffix first so all variants of a module share one stylesheet; returns the absolute path or `None`. `discover_variant_files` implements the head-precedence scheme defined by `_VARIANT_SUFFIXES` (plain .jac highest, then `.sv.jac`, `.cl.jac`, `.na.jac`): given a head file it returns all existing lower-precedence variants, and returns an empty list when a higher-precedence file exists (the caller is a variant, not the head) or when the file is an impl/test annex. `discover_base_file` inverts the mapping, resolving an `annex_path` back to its base module by checking the same directory, a module-named annex folder, and shared impl/test folders across the possible base extensions. Minimal CLI entry point for the jac command, handling cache purging locally and deferring everything else. `_get_cache_dir` returns the platform-appropriate global bytecode cache directory as a `Path` — LOCALAPPDATA-based on Windows, the Library caches folder on macOS, and XDG_CACHE_HOME (or ~/.cache) elsewhere. `_handle_purge` implements the purge subcommand: it prints usage and exits when a help flag is present in `sys.argv`, then walks the bytecode cache, the sibling bootstrap directory, and the unified JIR cache directory that supersedes them, tallying file counts and sizes before deleting each tree with `shutil.rmtree` (errors are reported to stderr without aborting the loop); it prints a summary of what was removed and always terminates the process via `sys.exit`. `start_cli` is the entry point proper: it dispatches to `_handle_purge` when the first argument is "purge" and otherwise lazily imports and delegates to the full CLI. Side effects: filesystem deletion of cache directories, stdout/stderr output, and process exit.

Structured generic types are encoded as tagged tuples built by `mk_list`, `mk_dict`, `mk_tuple`, and `mk_union`, recognized by the predicates `is_list_type`, `is_dict_type`, `is_tuple_type`, and `is_union_type`, unwrapped by `inner_types`, and rendered human-readably by `type_to_str`, which handles primitives, dataclass-based class infos, and nested tagged tuples recursively. Everything here is passive data plus pure helpers; nothing touches the graph.

The decorated `read_lock` and `write_lock` context managers wrap acquire/release in try/finally for exception-safe scoping. The lock is explicitly not reentrant: a thread acquiring it twice (or upgrading read to write) will deadlock.

Builds the Jac client runtime as a publishable npm package (name held in `RUNTIME_PKG_NAME`, "@jaseci/runtime"). Generators for the wheel metadata files produced by jac bundle. `generate_wheel_file` renders the .dist-info/WHEEL content, taking `generator_version`, a `pure_python` flag, and the `python_tag`/`abi_tag`/`platform_tag` triple that forms the compatibility tag. `generate_entry_points` builds entry_points.txt from a `JacConfig`, returning an empty string when the config has no [entrypoints] table. Three naming helpers derive canonical artifact names from `config`: `wheel_filename` (the PEP 427 .whl name, also parameterized by `python_tag`, `abi_tag`, and `platform_tag`), `dist_info_dirname` (the .dist-info directory name), and `sdist_filename` (the PEP 625 .tar.gz name); each raises ValueError when the project name is missing. All functions are pure string builders with no filesystem or graph side effects.

Package marker for the core Jaseci primitives package, which exists to host Jac `.jac` runtime modules. It contains no definitions of its own; the legacy `jaclang.runtimelib.runtime` import path is kept working through an alias installed in `jaclang.__init__`, which avoids eagerly compiling `.jac` sources during bootstrap. No parameters, return values, or graph side effects.

Request models for identity/credential authentication on the jaclang HTTP server, each parsed from untrusted JSON via a static `from_dict` that raises ValueError with a field-specific message on malformed input. `IdentityType` enumerates supported identity kinds (only `USERNAME` today) and `CredentialType` the credential kinds (only `PASSWORD`). `IdentityInput` pairs a `type` string with its raw `value`; `CredentialInput` pairs a `type` with a `password`. `LoginRequest` is the "POST /user/login" payload, requiring one `identity` and one `credential`; `RegisterRequest` is the "POST /user/register" payload, requiring a non-empty `identities` list plus a `credential`. All validation is pure — nothing is persisted and the graph is untouched.

Jac-specific builtins: the module that backs the language's implicitly available server-side helper surface, exported via `__all__`. Most runtime-backed names are provided lazily — a family of `_get_jac`, `_get_access_level`, `_get_llm`-style accessors fetches implementations from the runtime (`JacRuntimeInterface`, `AccessLevel`, `LLMModel`) on demand, and `__getattr__` resolves builtin names through them at attribute-access time so importing this module stays cheap. Two enums configure server features: `APIProtocol` (HTTP, WEBHOOK, or WEBSOCKET exposure for the `restspec` decorator, which attaches REST specs to a callable) and `ScheduleTrigger` (STATIC vs DYNAMIC trigger mode for the `schedule` decorator). Graph inspection comes from `printgraph`, which renders the graph from an optional `NodeArchetype` starting point with depth/traversal/format controls, and `_jac_graph_json`, its JSON counterpart. Two portability shims round it out: `new` is a portable constructor (plain instantiation on the server, lowering to the JS `new` semantics in client blocks), and `unsafe_html` wraps a string in a sentinel `dict` that client runtimes render as raw, unescaped HTML — callers must sanitise untrusted input first.

Package aggregator for the core client build plumbing: it re-exports the pieces of the toolchain — bun resolution (`get_bun`, `BUN_VERSION`), dependency checking (`ensure_client_deps`), asset handling (`AssetProcessor`), config access (`JacClientConfig`), import rewriting (`ImportProcessor`), the jac-to-js bridge (`JacToJSCompiler`), npm installation (`PackageInstaller`), Vite bundling (`ViteBundler`), route discovery (`RouteScanner`, `RouteEntry`), and compilation orchestration (`ViteCompiler`, `ViteClientBundleBuilder`, `make_client_bundle_builder`) — and pins the public surface via `__all__`. It defines nothing itself and has no side effects beyond importing its submodules.

Utilities for copying asset files between directories during client builds. `AssetProcessor` owns the work; its class-level `ASSET_EXTENSIONS` set enumerates the recognized asset suffixes (stylesheets, images, fonts, audio/video). `copy_assets` copies files whose suffix is in `ASSET_EXTENSIONS` from `src_dir` into `dest_dir`; `copy_typescript_files` does the same for TypeScript sources; and `copy_custom_asset_types` copies project-defined asset extensions. All three take a `preserve_structure` flag (default True) controlling whether the source directory layout is mirrored or files are flattened, return None, and side-effect only the filesystem — destination files are created or overwritten; the graph is untouched.

Document this Jac code:

```jac
"""Bun installer utility for jac-client.

Provides functions to resolve the bun binary path, auto-installing
a project-local copy to .jac/bin/ if bun is not on the system PATH.
"""

# Canonical pinned bun version. Single source of truth across the project
# (also reused by deployment targets that pre-install bun in container images).
# Bump this when a new bun release is validated.
glob BUN_VERSION = "1.3.11";

"""Resolve the path to the bun binary, auto-installing if needed.

Resolution order:
  1. System PATH (use the user's global bun if present)
  2. .jac/bin/bun (project-local, managed by jac)
  3. Auto-download to .jac/bin/ (silent, no prompt)

On success the resolved directory is prepended to PATH.
Returns the absolute path as a string, or None if unavailable.
"""
def get_bun -> str | None;

```

Bun installer utility for jac-client. `BUN_VERSION` pins the canonical bun release used across the project (including container-image deployment targets); bump it only after validating a new release. `get_bun` resolves the path to the bun binary, preferring the system PATH, then a project-local copy under .jac/bin/, and finally auto-downloading to .jac/bin/ silently with no prompt. On success it prepends the resolved directory to PATH (an environment side effect) and returns the absolute path as a string; it returns None when bun cannot be obtained. No graph side effects.

Orchestrates compilation of Vite client bundles. `ViteCompiler` is configured through `init` with the Vite workspace (`vite_package_json`, optional `vite_output_dir`, `vite_minify`, `runtime_path`) and three injected callbacks — `compile_to_js_func`, `extract_exports_func`, and `extract_globals_func` — that perform the actual jac-to-JS compilation and symbol extraction. Class constants list the router symbols re-exported to pages (`ROUTER_EXPORTS`) and the multi-part Jac suffixes (`COMPOUND_EXTENSIONS`). The pipeline compiles the shared runtime (`compile_runtime_utils`, `compile_pwa_runtime`), walks imports transitively via `compile_dependencies_recursively` (tracking `visited` paths and accumulating `collected_exports`/`collected_globals`), copies sibling JS/TS/asset files (`_copy_js_file`, `_copy_ts_file`, `_copy_asset_file`, `copy_root_assets`), emits WASM for native modules (`_emit_na_wasm`), writes source maps (`_write_source_map`), generates the Vite entry file (`create_entry_file`) plus a pages entry (`_create_pages_entry_content`, `_scan_and_compile_pages`) and a routes manifest (`_generate_routes_manifest`). `compile_and_bundle` runs the full compile of a `module` at `module_path` and returns the bundle outputs, while `compile` is the top-level entry returning the emitted artifact lists. Side effects are filesystem-only: compiled JS, entry files, manifests, and copied assets are written into the Vite output tree.

Configuration access for the Jac Client build plugin, loaded from the [plugins.client] section of jac.toml. The single class `JacClientConfig` extends `PluginConfigBase`, overriding `get_plugin_name`, `get_default_config`, and `load` to wire the base plumbing to the client section, with `save` persisting changes back. Around that core sit typed section getters — `get_api_config`, `get_base_path`, `get_vite_config`, `get_ts_config`, `get_configs`, `get_package_config`, `get_npm_config`, `get_paths_config`, and `get_pwa_config` (with `is_pwa_enabled` as a convenience predicate) — plus npm dependency management via `add_dependency` and `remove_dependency` (each taking a `name` and an `is_dev` flag). `check_runtime_version` compares the configured client runtime version against the installed one and `sync_runtime_version` writes the current version back. Entry point: construct a `JacClientConfig` and call the getters; everything else is internal to loading and persisting jac.toml state.

Implementation bodies for the three `AssetProcessor` copy methods; each shares the same shape — bail out if `src_dir` does not exist, create `dest_dir` (parents included), then run a nested `copy_recursive` walker over `source`/`destination` with `base` anchoring relative paths. When `preserve_structure` is True the file's `relative_path` under the base is mirrored into the destination; otherwise files are flattened to their bare names. Individual copy failures (OSError or shutil errors) are logged via `console.warning` and skipped rather than raised. `copy_custom_asset_types` first reads the client plugin's assets config through `get_config` and only copies files whose suffix is in the configured custom_extensions set (doing nothing when none are configured); `copy_typescript_files` matches the ".ts"/".tsx" suffixes; `copy_assets` matches the class's `ASSET_EXTENSIONS`. All return None; the only side effects are files written under `dest_dir` and warnings on the console.

Implementation of the client dependency checker. `ensure_client_deps` reads the package section from `config_loader` via `get_package_config` and returns True immediately when either the 'dependencies' or 'devDependencies' map has entries; otherwise it defers to `prompt_install_client_deps`. That helper explains on the console that npm packages are required, then asks "Install default client dependencies now? [Y/n]" — EOF/interrupt or a negative answer returns False (printing manual-setup hints). On consent it writes a default dependency set (react, react-dom, react-router-dom, form/validation libs) via `config_loader.add_dependency` with `is_dev=False`, the build tooling set (vite, typescript, type stubs) with `is_dev=True`, persists with `save`, and calls `invalidate` to drop cached config, returning True. Any failure while adding is caught, reported via `console.error`, and yields False. Side effects: terminal I/O and mutation of the project's jac.toml; no graph access.

Implementation slice of `ImportProcessor`, the piece of the Vite bundling pipeline that decides which client imports the Jac toolchain handles itself versus leaves to Vite. `should_process_import` is the policy: an `import_path` is ours when its suffix is '.jac' or '.js'; everything else (npm packages, CSS, etc.) falls through to Vite's own resolution. `process_vite_imports` walks the `imports` map of a compiled module's `ClientManifest` (when a `manifest` is present) and builds `imported_js_modules`, a list aligned with those imports: each '.js' or '.jac' entry contributes its `Path`, with failures (`FileNotFoundError` for JS, `ClientBundleError` for Jac) recorded as None placeholders instead of aborting. The `module_path` parameter identifies the module being bundled. Entry point is `process_vite_imports`, called by the compiler while assembling a bundle; the module itself performs no filesystem writes.

Implementation of `PackageInstaller`, which manages the project's npm packages by treating jac.toml as the source of truth. `init` binds the installer to a `project_dir`, creating a `JacClientConfig` as `config_loader` and recording the jac.toml path in `config_file`. `list_packages` loads the config and returns its 'dependencies' and 'devDependencies' maps. `install_package` adds `package_name` at `version` (defaulting to 'latest') via `add_dependency` with the `is_dev` flag, saves, then rebuilds; `uninstall_package` removes it via `remove_dependency` (raising `ClientBundleError` naming the missing package when absent), saves, then rebuilds; `install_all` just rebuilds from the current config. The shared rebuild step `_regenerate_and_install` resolves bun through `get_bun` (raising `ClientBundleError` if unavailable), regenerates package.json with a `ViteBundler` via `create_package_json`, temporarily materializes a root package.json (`_ensure_root_package_json`), runs bun install in the project (raising on a non-zero exit), and always cleans up via `_cleanup_root_package_files`. Every public method first verifies `config_file` exists and raises `ClientBundleError` telling the user to run "jac init" otherwise. Side effects: mutates jac.toml, regenerates package.json, and installs node modules; no graph access.

Implements `RouteScanner`, the filesystem-convention router for Jac client pages: it models a pages directory tree as React Router routes. `postinit` derives `pages_dir` from `project_root` and `PAGES_DIR_NAME`, and `has_pages_dir` gates everything. The entry point is `scan`, which resets internal state, recurses via `_scan_directory`, checks duplicates with `_detect_collisions`, and returns `RouteEntry` records; `get_layouts` (layouts keyed by URL prefix) and `get_page_files` expose the side products of the last scan. `_scan_directory` walks entries in sorted order for determinism: parenthesized directories are route groups that add no URL segment but can force `auth_required` (when the group matches `AUTH_GROUP_NAME`), ordinary directories extend `url_prefix`, and `.jac` files become routes unless they carry one of `SKIP_SUFFIXES`. A file matching `LAYOUT_FILENAME` becomes a layout wrapper (`is_layout` True) rather than a route, with duplicate layouts for one prefix raising `ClientBundleError`; a file matching `INDEX_FILENAME` maps to its directory's path. Naming is handled by `_file_to_route_path`, which converts filename stems to route segments (bracketed names become ':param' segments, catch-all names become '*' and set `is_catch_all`), and `_file_to_component_name`, which builds a unique import identifier from the path using `COMPONENT_PREFIX`, skipping group directories and stripping brackets. `_detect_collisions` raises `ClientBundleError` when two non-layout files claim the same `path`. Read-only over the filesystem; state lives on the scanner instance.

Implementation of the Vite-backed client bundle builder. `make_client_bundle_builder` is the shared constructor: given an optional `base_path` (otherwise derived from the runtime's base directory, upgraded to the project root via `find_project_root` when one exists), it creates a `ViteBundler`, ensures a generated package.json exists under the client dir's configs folder (generating one with `create_package_json` and raising `ClientBundleError` if that fails), and returns a `ViteClientBundleBuilder` wired to that package.json with output under the client dist directory and `vite_minify` off. On the builder itself, `init` stores `vite_output_dir`, `vite_package_json`, `vite_minify`, and a lazy `_compiler` slot after delegating `runtime_path` to the superclass. `_get_compiler` builds the `ViteCompiler` on first use — raising `ClientBundleError` when `vite_package_json` is missing — injecting `_compile_to_js`, `_extract_client_exports`, and `_extract_client_globals` as its callbacks. `_compile_bundle` overrides the simple-concatenation strategy: it runs the compiler's `compile_and_bundle` on the `module` and `module_path` and wraps the result in a `ClientBundle` carrying `module_name`, `code`, `client_functions`, `client_globals`, and `hash`. `cleanup_temp_dir` removes the compiled directory next to the package.json, logging (not raising) via `console.warning` on failure. Side effects are filesystem-only: generated configs, bundle output, and temp-dir removal.

Declares `ImportProcessor`, the component of the Jac-to-Vite build that handles client imports. `process_vite_imports` takes the compiled module's `manifest` (a `ClientManifest`, or None when the module has none) plus the `module_path` being bundled and returns a list of resolved import paths, using None entries for imports that could not be processed. `should_process_import` is the filter predicate deciding whether a given `import_path` should be compiled/copied by the Jac toolchain rather than left for Vite to resolve. The `ClientManifest` type is imported only under TYPE_CHECKING, so this declaration file adds no runtime import cost; failures during processing surface as `ClientBundleError`. Method bodies live in the companion impl file.

Declares `JacToJSCompiler`, the object that fronts Jac-to-JavaScript compilation for the client build. It is constructed around three injected callables held as fields: `_compile_to_js` (compiles a source `Path` to a JS string plus optional loaded module), `_extract_client_exports`, and `_extract_client_globals`. `compile_module` compiles the file at `module_path` and returns the JS text, the module object (or None), and its `ClientManifest` (or None). `extract_exports` lists client-exported names from a `manifest`; `extract_globals` gathers client global values from the `manifest` and live `module`; `add_runtime_imports` rewrites compiled `js_code` to include the client runtime imports and returns the new string. `ClientManifest` is imported only under TYPE_CHECKING, keeping runtime imports light. Pure computation over injected behavior; no graph or filesystem side effects in this declaration.

File-based route scanner implementing the pages-directory convention. `RouteEntry` is one derived route: its URL `path`, the generated `component_import` identifier, the source `file_path`, plus flags `auth_required`, `is_layout`, and `is_catch_all`, and a `children` list for nesting. `RouteScanner` walks a project's pages folder (derived from `project_root` in `postinit` as `pages_dir`); class constants pin the convention — `PAGES_DIR_NAME`, `LAYOUT_FILENAME`, `INDEX_FILENAME`, `AUTH_GROUP_NAME`, the `COMPONENT_PREFIX` for import names, and `SKIP_SUFFIXES` for non-page Jac files. `has_pages_dir` reports whether there is anything to scan; `scan` produces the route list while filling the private `_routes`, `_layouts`, and `_page_files` caches read back via `get_layouts` and `get_page_files`. Internals: `_scan_directory` recurses with a `url_prefix` and inherited `auth_required`, `_file_to_route_path` converts a filename stem into a route segment, `_file_to_component_name` builds the unique import name, and `_detect_collisions` rejects duplicate paths. Read-only filesystem traversal; state is kept on the scanner instance.

Vite bundling for jac-client, centered on the `ViteBundler` class plus module-level constants: `API_BASE_URL_ENV_VAR` (env var threading the API base URL through deep call chains), `JAC_API_BASE_URL_KEY` (the globalThis key injected at build time), dev-server readiness knobs (`VITE_READY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, `VITE_READY_PATTERNS`, `VITE_URL_PATTERNS`), and `CONFIG_META_KEYS` (config-generator-internal keys never written to output). `init` ties a bundler to a `project_dir` with optional `output_dir`, `minify`, and `config_path`. One axis is config generation: `create_vite_config` (parameterized by `entry_file`, an `api_base_url_override`, `is_dev`, `api_port`, and mobile HMR settings) with formatting helpers (`_generate_vite_config_content`, `_format_plugin_options`, `_format_config_object`, `_format_define_entries`), plus `create_package_json`, `create_tsconfig`, `create_config_files` (from jac.toml's client configs section), and `create_npmrc`. A second axis is production builds: `build` runs Vite on an `entry_file`, and `find_bundle`, `find_css`, and `read_bundle` locate and read the emitted artifacts. The third axis is development: `start_dev_server` launches Vite as a subprocess on a `port` (optionally capturing output until ready via `_start_vite_with_output_capture`, with `_ensure_dev_index_html` and `_ensure_dev_dependencies` preparing the build dir), and `_ensure_root_package_json`/`_cleanup_root_package_files` temporarily materialize root-level package files around bun/Vite invocations. Errors surface as `ClientBundleError`. Entry points for callers are `build`, `start_dev_server`, and the create_* generators.

Vite-enhanced client bundle generation. `ViteClientBundleBuilder` extends `ClientBundleBuilder` to replace simple concatenation with optimized Vite bundling: `init` takes the optional `runtime_path`, `vite_output_dir`, and `vite_package_json` plus a `vite_minify` flag; `_get_compiler` lazily constructs the underlying `ViteCompiler`; `_compile_bundle` compiles a `module` at `module_path` into a `ClientBundle`; and `cleanup_temp_dir` removes the intermediate compiled directory. `make_client_bundle_builder` is the single shared construction point (used by both the core `get_client_bundle_builder` hook default and the jac-client build targets): `base_path` names the project root, resolved from the active runtime's base path when None, and the builder's `.jac/client/configs/package.json` is generated on demand. Errors surface as `ClientBundleError`. Side effects: writes generated configs and bundle output under the project's client directory.

Core utilities for generating client bundles for Jac web front-ends. `ClientBundleError` is the failure type. `_lookup_module_in_hub` finds a compiled module by `path_key` in a single program's `hub` (returning None on miss; the bundler deliberately never spans programs), and `_ensure_js_generated` reruns the ES generation pass for a `mod` whose JS is missing (a Windows initial-compile quirk). `ClientBundle` is the result container: `module_name`, the bundled `code`, the `client_functions` and `client_globals` name lists, and a content `hash`; `_CachedBundle` pairs a bundle with the source `signature` it was built from. `ClientBundleBuilder` is the shared base for builders: `build` compiles a `module` to a `ClientBundle`, short-circuiting through `_cache` unless `force` is set; `_extract_client_exports` and `_extract_client_globals` read the client surface out of a `ClientManifest`; `_compile_to_js` compiles one `source_path`; and the static `_signature` fingerprints a set of paths for cache keys. Concrete bundling lives in `_compile_bundle`, supplied by the jac-client plugin's Vite/Bun builder — the base implementation raises if invoked standalone.

The client-side runtime for Jac JSX and walker interactions — the module a compiled client page executes against, built on React. Rendering starts at `__jacJsx`, the JSX factory every lowered view calls, producing a `JsxElement`. A block of public globals re-exports the React and React Router surface (`useState`, `useEffect`, `Router`, `Routes`, `Route`, `Link`, `Navigate`, `useNavigate`, `useLocation`, `useParams`, `Outlet`) for auto-injection into `has` state and entry/exit effects, alongside `JacClientErrorBoundary` (the react-error-boundary `ErrorBoundary`) and `JacSchema`, a zod-backed schema helper built by `__createJacSchema`; `useRouter` and `navigate` give imperative routing. Server interaction is the second pillar: `jacSpawn`/`__jacSpawn` spawn walkers over HTTP, `__jacCallFunction` invokes server functions, and the auth suite (`jacSignup`, `jacLogin`, `jacLogout`, `jacIsLoggedIn`, with `__normalizeIdentity`/`__normalizeCredential` coercing username/password shorthands into typed identity/credential shapes) manages sessions, persisted through the localStorage helpers (`__getLocalStorage`, `__setLocalStorage`, `__removeLocalStorage`) and gated in the UI by `AuthGuard`. Compiler-driven auto-caching wraps those calls: `__cachedEndpointCall` consults `__cacheGet`/`__cacheSet`/`__isFresh`/`__evictOldest` keyed state and falls through to `__doWalkerFetch` or `__doFuncFetch`, while `__invalidateEndpoint` and `__overlaps` implement effect-based invalidation from `__getEndpointEffects`. UI conveniences include `JacAwaiting` (the compile-time wrapper for try/awaiting clauses, currently a thin layer over React Suspense), `ErrorFallback` and `errorOverlay` for failure display, and `useJacForm`/`JacForm` for react-hook-form + zod forms. Finally, client error reporting ships failures to the server: `__jacReportError` posts a message with stacks (including React's `componentStack`), `__jacInstallErrorHandlers` hooks global handlers, and `__jacReactErrorHandler` is the onError wired into `JacClientErrorBoundary`.

Implementation of the base client bundling pipeline. `_lookup_module_in_hub` finds a compiled `Module` for `path_key` in a single program's `hub`, retrying with case/separator normalization for Windows; it is deliberately single-hub so the bundler never reuses a module parked in the internal program whose JS state may be incomplete — on a miss callers recompile fresh. `_ensure_js_generated` runs `EsastGenPass` when a module's JS is absent (Windows can skip the ES pass on initial compile). On `ClientBundleBuilder`: `postinit` defaults `runtime_path` to the bundled client runtime file next to this module; `build` maps the Python `module` back to its Jac source, fetches or compiles the compiled module, gathers the source plus its `client_manifest` imports into the path set fingerprinted by `_signature` (a sha256 over per-file mtimes, tolerating missing files), and returns the cached bundle when the signature matches unless `force` is set, otherwise delegating to `_compile_bundle` and caching the result in `_cache` as a `_CachedBundle`. `_extract_client_exports` returns the manifest's export names deduplicated and sorted; `_extract_client_globals` resolves each manifest global from recorded values, then live `module` attributes, else None, returning a sorted dict. `_compile_to_js` compiles `source_path` through the active program, raising `ClientBundleError` listing any new compile errors, and ensures JS generation before returning the code and module. The base `_compile_bundle` always raises `ClientBundleError` — concrete bundling comes from the jac-client plugin's Vite/Bun override. Side effects: compilation populates the shared program hub and the builder's in-memory cache; nothing is written to disk here.

Implementation bodies for `ExecutionContext`. `postinit` has two paths: with `_parent` set it is a per-request fork that shares the parent's `mem` and `system_root` (plus app identity) while leaving reports/call state request-local; otherwise it snapshots `base_path_dir` and `full_target_path` from the runtime's bootstrap seeds when unset — locking the persistence path at construction so later seed mutations by sibling clients cannot leak in — builds a `TieredMemory` (no L3 persistence when `base_path_dir` is None, which keeps tests fast), loads the system root by its fixed `SUPER_ROOT_UUID` or creates and stores a fresh `Root` anchor, and defaults `user_root` and `entry_node` to `system_root`. `_get_anchor` resolves an `anchor_id` through `mem` and raises ValueError unless it yields a `NodeAnchor`. `set_user_root` installs the anchor for `root_id` as the permission/ownership boundary and resets `entry_node` to it; `set_entry_node` picks the given anchor or falls back to `user_root`. `close` syncs and closes the memory tiers, but is a no-op on forks since the backend belongs to the parent. `get_root` returns the current user's `Root` archetype. `_aget_anchor`, `aset_user_root`, and `aset_entry_node` mirror their sync counterparts through the async Memory surface so the event loop never blocks on storage reads. Side effects: graph persistence writes when creating the system root, and storage tier shutdown on `close`.

Implementation of `QueryPlan`'s introspection surface — the piece of the query planner that lets a plan describe itself. `is_trivial` reports a no-op plan (empty `chain`, no `field_predicates`, no `id_in`, no `node_type_final`); the planner treats such plans as load-everything and typically refuses them. `needs` computes the set of capability strings a storage backend must declare to run the plan unassisted: 'type_pushdown' when a final node type or any typed hop in `chain` is present, 'field_pushdown' for `field_predicates`, 'id_in' for identifier narrowing, and 'slice' when `slc` is set. The planner compares a backend's declared capabilities against this set — a superset takes the plan as-is, otherwise unmet needs are stripped and applied above a reduced plan. `repr` renders a compact debug string (root prefix from `root_id`, hop chain with `edge_type`/`direction`/`node_type`, type filter, predicates, id-set size, slice bounds) used by the JAC_QUERY_TRACE facility. All three are pure reads of plan state with no side effects; entry points are the planner's routing logic and trace logging.

Implementation of the Jac test harness. `JacTestCheck.add_test` registers a test: it normalizes `filepath` by stripping the test/module suffixes, indexes a new `TestSuite` record (wrapping `test_func` in a unittest `FunctionTestCase`, keyed by `func_name` with an optional `display_name`) under `test_suite_path`, and adds the case to the global `test_suite`. `run_test` selects what to run — the whole suite, one file's cases, and/or a single `func_name` — then executes it with a `JacTextTestRunner` configured by `maxfail`, the `xit` fail-fast flag, and `verbose`; on failure it bumps `failcount` and sets `breaker` when the failure budget is exhausted. `reset` clears both the suite and the per-file index. `JacTextTestRunner.init` stores `max_failures` and `_makeResult` returns a `JacTestResult`, which counts failures (`failures_count`), flips `shouldStop` via `stop` once `max_failures` is reached, and seeds its count from `failcount` in `postinit`. `parametrize` mirrors pytest-style parametrization: for each value in `params` it derives an id (via `id_fn` or str), builds a closure over the parameter, and registers an individual test against the caller's file under `base_name`. declarative dict belongs in the post-filter the runtime applies above.

  - `'field_pushdown'`  — backend can apply declarative field predicates

  - `'slice'`           — backend can apply `(offset, limit)` natively

        self: Storage, source: str, destination: (str | BinaryIO | None) = None
    ) -> (bytes | None) abs;

    """Delete a file or directory from storage."""
    def delete(self: Storage, path: str) -> bool abs;

    """Check if a path exists in storage."""
    def exists(self: Storage, path: str) -> bool abs;

    """List files in storage.

    Args:
        prefix: Filter results to paths starting with this prefix
        recursive: If True, list files in subdirectories

    Yields:
        File paths relative to the storage root
    """
    def list_files(
        self: Storage, prefix: str = "", recursive: bool = False
    ) -> Generator[str, None, None] abs;

    """Get metadata for a file (size, modified, created, is_dir, name)."""
    def get_metadata(self: Storage, path: str) -> dict[str, any] abs;

    """Copy a file within storage."""
    def copy(self: Storage, source: str, destination: str) -> bool abs;

    """Move a file within storage."""
    def move(self: Storage, source: str, destination: str) -> bool abs;

    """Return a public or pre-signed URL for the given path.

    Args:
        path: Storage path/key
        expires_in: Seconds until signed URL expires (None = use backend default,
                    ignored for public buckets)

    Returns:
        HTTP/HTTPS URL the client can fetch directly.
    """
    def get_url(self: Storage, path: str, expires_in: (int | None) = 3600) -> str abs;
}

```

Base storage abstraction for Jac: `Storage` is the abstract interface for file/blob operations that plugins (such as jac-scale) override with cloud backends. `upload` stores a `source` (local path or file-like object) at a `destination` key with optional `metadata`, returning the stored path or URL. `download` retrieves `source` — returning bytes when `destination` is None, otherwise writing to the given path or stream and returning None. `delete` removes a file or directory at `path` and `exists` tests presence, both returning `bool`. `list_files` yields root-relative paths filtered by `prefix`, descending into subdirectories only when `recursive` is set. `get_metadata` reports size, timestamps, directory flag, and name for a `path`; `copy` and `move` duplicate or relocate entries within storage. `get_url` returns a public or pre-signed HTTP(S) URL for `path`, with `expires_in` controlling signed-URL lifetime (None defers to the backend default and is ignored for public buckets). Every method is abstract; side effects depend entirely on the concrete backend.

Test-framework constructs for Jac, layered on unittest. `JacTestResult` extends the text result with fail-budget accounting: it carries the runner's `stream`/`descriptions`/`verbosity`, an optional `max_failures` cap, and a `failures_count` seeded in `postinit`; `addFailure` increments the count and `stop` halts the run once the cap is hit. `JacTextTestRunner` accepts `max_failures` in `init` and overrides `_makeResult` to produce a `JacTestResult`. `JacTestCheck` is the global registry: a class-level `test_suite`, a `test_suite_path` map from source file to registered `TestSuite` records (each pairing a `test_case` with its `func_name` and `display_name`), plus `breaker` and `failcount` counters shared across runs. Its statics `add_test`, `run_test` (filtered by `filepath` and/or `func_name`, with `xit` fail-fast, `maxfail`, and `verbose` options), and `reset` manage registration, execution, and teardown. `parametrize` registers one test per value in `params` under `base_name`, deriving ids via `id_fn`, mirroring pytest-style parametrization. Side effects are limited to the class-level registry and unittest execution state.

In-process test client for Jac API servers, in the spirit of Flask's test client and FastAPI's TestClient: requests are executed against the server handler directly, with no sockets or ports. `TestResponse` wraps a response for assertions — `status_code`, `headers`, raw `text`, a cached `json` accessor, plus derived getters `ok` and `data`. `JacTestClient` is built via the static `from_file`, which compiles and serves a `jac_file` with an optional `base_path` (isolating persistence), `module_name`, and `config`; initialization is lazy through `_ensure_initialized`. HTTP-style verbs `get`, `post`, and `put` (and the general `request`) accept a `path` with optional `params`, JSON body, and `headers`, funneling through `_execute_request` and `_parse_response` to produce a `TestResponse`. Authentication is first-class: `register_user` and `login` hit the user endpoints with a `username`/`password` and store the session, while `set_auth_token` and `clear_auth` manage the bearer token (`_auth_token`) attached to subsequent requests. The `server` and `user_manager` getters expose the underlying `JacAPIServer` internals, `reload` re-initializes after source changes, and `close` tears the server down — tests should call it to release persistence resources.
