Cached dataclass field-type introspection. `get_field_types` returns the field-name-to-resolved-annotation map for a dataclass `cls`, resolving forward references through typing's hint machinery and falling back to raw annotations when resolution fails (circular imports); non-dataclass inputs yield an empty dict. Results are cached per class because hint resolution is extremely expensive (~350 microseconds per call) and would otherwise dominate deserialization when many anchors of the same class are processed. `invalidate` evicts one class's cached entry — needed after an HMR reload redefines a class — and `clear` empties the whole cache. Side effects are limited to the module-level cache.

Helper utilities for Jac constructs, mixing declared helpers with two small inline ones. `sys_path_context` is a context manager that temporarily adds `path` to the import search path. Graph inspection support: `collect_node_connections` accumulates a node's reachable `connections` and `edge_ids` from `current_node` while tracking `visited_nodes`, and `traverse_graph` drives the bounded printgraph walk from `nd` with depth control (`cur_depth`/`depth`), `edge_type` filtering, BFS/DFS switching (`bfs`, `dfs`, `queue`), per-node depth bookkeeping (`node_depths`), and `node_limit`/`edge_limit` caps. Compiler-side helpers `extract_type` and `extract_params` pull type names and call parameters out of unitree nodes, while `is_instance` and `all_issubclass` generalize instance/subclass checks over unions and tuples of types. Persistence plumbing: `storage_key` renders an anchor UUID as its storage key string, `to_uuid` normalizes a string-or-UUID `id`, `get_name` derives the project name from an adjacent jac.toml (using `target_path`, or the bootstrap seed when omitted — per-context owners such as an ExecutionContext should pass it explicitly to stay independent of ambient seed state), and `get_db_path` builds the database file path under `base_path`, keyed by project name for projects or filename for standalone files, forwarding `target_path` to `get_name`. Aside from the sys.path mutation inside the context manager, these are read-only helpers.

File system watching for Jac's HMR support, built on the watchdog library. `ChangeType` classifies events as CREATED, MODIFIED, or DELETED, and `FileChangeEvent` records one change: the `path`, its `change_type`, and a `timestamp`. `JacFileWatcher` owns the loop: it observes `watch_paths`, matching filenames against `pattern` (Jac sources by default) plus `additional_patterns` covering frontend assets (TS/JS, styles, images). Rapid successive changes are debounced via `_debounce_ms`, with candidate events parked in `_pending_events` and flushed by `_debounce_flush`; `_last_flush` and `_running` track loop state and `_observer` holds the watchdog observer. `start` and `stop` control the lifecycle, consumers subscribe with `add_callback`/`remove_callback` (stored in `_callbacks`), and internals `_on_change`, `_matches_pattern`, and `_notify_callbacks` route raw events through filtering to the registered callbacks. Side effects: background observer threads and callback invocation; nothing touches the graph.

Language tooling for the Jaclang project, declared around three constructs. `AstKidInfo` describes one child slot of an AST node — its `name`, type string `typ`, and optional default. `UniNodeInfo` holds metadata about unitree node classes: it wraps a `cls`, maintains the class-level `type_map` registry from names to node types, and its `postinit`/`process` populate that registry from the node class hierarchy. `AstTool` is the command surface built on top: after `init`, `pass_template` renders a skeleton for writing a new compiler pass over the node catalog, `py_uni_nodes` lists the Python-AST-to-unitree correspondence, `ir` renders a program's intermediate representations per its `args` (leveraging the imported ES backend and unparse helpers for JS views), and `autodoc_uninode` generates reference documentation for the unitree node classes. These tools are read-only over compiler structures; they produce strings for CLI/docs consumption.

Symbol table testing helpers for Jaseci — assertion utilities test suites use to verify compiler symbol tables. `look_down` searches a `UniScopeNode` for `name` in `names_in_scope` and, when `deep` is set, recurses through `kid_scope` child scopes, returning the `Symbol` or None. `assert_symbol_exists` wraps that lookup for a `symbol_name`, failing the test when absent and optionally checking that `symbol_type` appears in the symbol's string form, then returns the symbol for chaining. Location checks parse the symbol's string representation: `assert_symbol_decl_at` verifies the declaration sits at a given `line`/`col`, `assert_symbol_defns_at` checks every (line, col) pair in `expected_defns`, and `assert_symbol_uses_at` does the same against the symbol's `uses`. `assert_symbol_complete` composes existence, declaration, definitions, and uses checks in one call. `assert_sub_table_exists` verifies a child scope whose `scope_name` contains `table_name` and whose type matches `tab_type`, returning the matching `UniScopeNode`. All functions are pure checks that raise AssertionError with diagnostic messages on mismatch; no state is modified.

Builder-pipeline job management for the studio backend — the Jac port of the old Python builders module. It models the 13 dataset build stages listed in `BUILDERS` (from "seed_conversion" through "verify_dataset") as detached jac run subprocesses over the shared jobs plumbing: `jobs.launch` spawns the stage with an exit marker and a job file, `jobs.live_status` resolves status live from the run log's __EXIT__ marker and pid liveness, and `metrics.tail` supplies recent log output. `BuilderView` is the client-facing shape for one stage: `stage`, `status`, `pid`, `run_id`, `started`, a `log_tail`, and an optional `message`. Path helpers `_job_file` and `_run_log` place per-stage job/log files under the results directory's _builder folder, and `_build_status` assembles a `BuilderView` from them (coercing the job dict's untyped pid through int-of-str per the 0.16.1 checker notes). The two public endpoints are `list_builders`, returning live views for all stages in `BUILDERS` order, and `run_builder`, which validates the `stage` against the list and `jobs.safe` (names are embedded in a shell command), refuses when already running, takes the heavy lock via `jobs.heavy_acquire` (reporting what it is busy with otherwise), truncates stale state by relaunching with a fresh run log, and spawns the stage with the project venv's bin prepended to PATH and cwd at the data root. Side effects: detached subprocesses plus job/log files on disk.

Streaming chat endpoint for the studio, served as Server-Sent Events. `chat_stream` takes the conversation `messages`, a `model_id`, and sampling knobs (`temperature`, `top_p`, `max_tokens`); it validates the model via `models.model_by_id` and `models.model_available`, yielding a single error frame for an unknown or not-on-disk model, then delegates to `inference.stream_chat` with the resolved model path — that generator holds one lock across load and generation so a concurrent request cannot swap the resident model mid-stream, and emits its own error frame on failure. Frames are dicts keyed by "kind": one "load" frame (load time and model), a "token" frame per generated token, a final "done" frame (full text, token count, throughput, timings), or "error". Chat persistence is deliberately not done here; the client calls separate persistence walkers. `stop_generation` cancels an in-flight generation by `gen_id` (from the stream's load frame, defaulting to the current one) through `inference.request_cancel`, returning whether anything was stopped — it is lock-free by design, since the streaming generator owns the model lock and this cancellation flag is what actually frees the GPU (client-side reader cancellation alone left decoding running to the token limit).

`AppShell` — the root client component (public, no auth; rendered as the app's entry, not an HTTP route). Takes no props. It renders the studio shell: `NavRail` twice (top workspace switcher, side section rail) plus all section instances for the three workspaces, kept permanently mounted and shown/hidden via the `slot` CSS helper so per-section state — including an in-flight chat SSE stream — survives switching. State: `workspace` ("01"/"02"/"03", restored from the "jacml.workspace" localStorage key, defaulting to "03" on first visit and written back by `goWorkspace`), a per-workspace `sections` map updated immutably by `go`, and backend liveness in `online`. Server interaction is a single call: the entry effect and the 3-second interval stored in `probeId` invoke `probe`, which awaits the sv-imported `system_ram` endpoint purely as a health check — success sets online, any thrown error marks the backend offline. Response states: while `online` is unknown the shell renders a connecting `EmptyState`; when the probe fails it renders `Offline` with an onRetry that re-probes immediately; when online it renders the full layout, passing each workspace's Chat its scoped history and default model from `WS_DEFAULT_MODEL`. Side effects on mount: adds the antialiased class to the document body, applies the stored light/dark mode from the "jacml.mode" key before first paint, and clears the interval on exit. Error cases beyond the offline card are swallowed: all localStorage access is wrapped in try/except so storage-denied browsers degrade gracefully.
