Backend-offline status card, the Jac port of the old offline component. Purely presentational: a dashed-border card announcing the backend is down, showing the command to start the server and noting the automatic retry cadence — AppShell owns the actual retry-every-3s loop and swaps this component out as soon as the probe succeeds. The single optional parameter `onRetry` is a no-argument callback; when provided, a RETRY NOW `Button` is rendered whose click handler fires it for an immediate re-probe, and when omitted the button row is not rendered at all. Returns the card as a `JsxElement`; no state, no side effects.

`Composer` — public client component (no auth; a UI entry, not an HTTP route) for the chat input area. Request shape (props): the controlled textarea `value`; `busy`, whether a generation is in flight; `categories`, a list of prompt-category dicts whose "id" labels the chips; and four callbacks — `onSet` (textarea change), `onSend` (submit, receiving the current text), `onStop` (cancel while busy), and `onChip` (a chip's category id). Response: a `JsxElement` — a chip row above a rounded container holding an auto-growing transparent textarea (row count from `_rows`, which clamps the newline count between 1 and 8) and one action `Button` that reads STOP while `busy` and SEND otherwise. Behavior/edge cases: Enter sends (Shift+Enter inserts a newline via the guarded keydown handler); the button is disabled when idle with only whitespace in `value`, but never disabled while `busy` so a stream can always be stopped; clicking it while busy calls `onStop`, otherwise `onSend`. No server calls or side effects of its own — everything is delegated to the callbacks.

Model picker for the chat header: a rounded pill plus a COMPARE popover, porting the old model-pill component and replacing a plain select. `ModelPill` is the public entry: given the registered `models`, the primary `modelId`, the active `compareId`, plus load state (`loadedId` for the resident model, `loadingId`/`loadElapsed` while one warms, `loadError` text) and the `onPick`/`onPickCompare` callbacks, it renders the header row with two independent popovers gated by local `pickerOpen`/`cmpOpen` state. The pill button shows the current model's label — or a live "loading … {seconds}s" readout while `loadingId` is set — and opens a panel listing every model with a status badge: LOADED for the resident one, its size in GB when available but cold, MISSING when not on disk; unavailable entries are disabled. Picking calls `onPick` and closes. The COMPARE side (label suffixed ON when a `compareId` is active) opens its own panel offering an off row plus every eligible target, and selection flows through `onPickCompare` so the next send streams both models side-by-side; the active vs-model and any truncated `loadError` are surfaced inline. Helpers: `_label` resolves a model id to its display label (falling back to the id) and `_cmp_opts` filters `models` to available non-primary compare candidates. Popovers are hand-rolled — a relative trigger, an absolute panel, and a fixed transparent overlay that closes on outside click — with no Radix dependency; opening one popover closes the other. All effects go through the two callbacks.

Chat right rail: the prompt library plus last-run stats panel (a port of the old rail component; sampling controls are gone since the server now supplies defaults). `Rail` receives the `prompts` category list, a `lastStats` dict (or None), a `collapsed` flag, and callbacks `onPick` (fired with a chosen prompt string) and `onToggle` (collapse/expand). When `collapsed` it renders only a thin edge button that calls `onToggle`; expanded, it renders a fixed-width column with a header (toggle in the corner), an accordion of prompt categories driven by the `openCat` state (defaulting to the "py2jac" category, toggling closed when its header is clicked again) where each open category lists its prompts as truncated one-liners — `_trunc` keeps only the first line, capped at 54 characters with an ellipsis, while the full prompt remains in the hover title — and clicking one fires `onPick`. Below a dashed rule, the LAST RUN block prints tokens-per-second, token count, and generation/load seconds from `lastStats`, or a "no run yet" line when absent. Purely presentational; all behavior is delegated to the two callbacks.

`Sidebar` — public client component (no auth; not an HTTP route) for the chat history rail. Props (request shape): `chats`, newest-first records grouped by their `updated_at` day via `_groups`; `activeId` highlighting the open chat; `ramGb`/`residentGb` feeding the footer memory gauge; `todayIso` so the current day's group is labeled TODAY instead of its ISO date; `busy`, which disables the new-chat `Button`, dims rows, and suppresses open/rename/delete while a generation runs; and callbacks `onNew`, `onOpen` (chat id), `onDelete` (chat id), and `onRename` (id plus new title). Response: a `JsxElement` sidebar — new-chat button, day-grouped rows (an empty-state line when there are no chats), and the MEM gauge. Row behavior: hovering reveals REN/DEL ghost buttons (click-stopped so they don't open the chat); REN enters inline-edit mode via `startEdit`, holding `editingId` and `draft` state, where Enter or blur runs `commitRename` — which calls `onRename` only for a non-empty trimmed title and always exits edit mode — and Escape cancels without committing. Untitled chats render as "untitled". The footer `_mem_gauge` (a props-object component per the compile convention, taking `used`/`total` in one dict) prints resident vs total RAM and an 8-cell bar built by `_repeat`, clamping the filled-cell count to 0-8 and guarding division by a zero total. Error cases are purely defensive UI: all mutations route through the callbacks, so the component itself performs no server calls.

The chat message thread, porting the old thread component to Jac. It models a conversation as asymmetric bubbles — user messages as right-aligned pills, assistant messages as left-aligned blocks — with COMPARE mode rendering two assistant replies that share a `pairGroup` side-by-side in dashed panes labelled per model. Content is split by `_codeParts` on triple-backtick fences into text and code segments: code goes to the shared `CodeBlock` pane (language taken from the fence's first line) and prose renders through react-markdown with GFM support instead of a preformatted paragraph, so headers, bold, lists, tables, and links actually format. The `MD_COMPONENTS` map supplies that renderer's element overrides — the `_mdH1`..`_mdTd` family maps each markdown element onto the app's semantic design tokens, deliberately avoiding the Tailwind Typography plugin. Row assembly is `_rows`: it walks `messages`, remembering the most recent user prompt so each row carries the "user" text that produced it (used when saving examples), and pairing consecutive assistant messages with matching pair groups into 2-up rows. `Bubble` renders one message: streaming placeholder and blinking cursor while `streaming`, the segment list, an inline error box, a stats footer line (tok/s, tokens, timings), and — for a finished assistant reply with both prompt and content — a save button that calls `onSave` with the prompt/response pair and flips brief `saved` feedback. `Thread` is the entry point: given `messages`, a model-id-to-label `labels` map (resolved by `lbl`), and `onSave`, it renders the scrollable column with an empty-state hint and auto-scrolls to the chat-end anchor whenever `messages` changes.

`CptData` — public client section component (workspace 03; read-only, no auth beyond the app's session) that browses the continual-pretrain corpus. Server surface consumed: `cpt_manifest` (fetched once on entry; response is a dict whose "ok" gate guards rendering and whose "sources", "packed", "gate", "decontam", plus scalar fields like "total_tokens", "seq_len", "split", "eos_token", and "n_repos" feed the panels), and the `cpt_files`/`cpt_rows` pair wrapped by the `useRowPager` hook (25 rows per page, first file opened on mount) driving the `RowBrowser` over the raw per-source files and packed splits. Rendering: `_tiles` shows a total-tokens `StatTile` plus one tile per source (token counts compacted by `_k`, which renders 1970952 as "1.97M"); `_composition` draws the stacked token-composition bar as plain divs — each source is pre-tagged with a shade from the `SHADES` foreground-opacity ramp during entry so the JSX loops never need an index — with a legend beneath; `_gate` renders the per-repo code-gate table (files/passed/percent) and a footer summing decontamination drops and echoing the packed train/valid counts and sequencing settings. Error/loading cases: until the manifest resolves (or when "ok" is false) the tile area shows a loading label and the composition/gate panels render empty; there are no mutations — the section is strictly read-only over the dataset on disk.

Results view for the workspace-03 CPT experiments: a side-by-side read of the two runs named in `RUNS` ("cpt-v1", "cpt-v2"), showing per-run status, iteration progress, final losses, and both loss curves. `CptResults` fetches `get_all_cpt_status` — the same source the TRAIN section polls — exactly once per activation (the entry effect keyed on `active`), on the reasoning that results only move while a run is training, which TRAIN watches live; failures are swallowed and the `loadedOnce` flag gates the loading state. Rendering centers on the inner `RunBlock` props-component: for a run `name` it pulls that run's dict out of the fetched map (falling back to an `EmptyState` when absent) and lays out the run title with a `StatusGlyph` and optional message, three `StatTile`s (iterations out of total, final train loss, final val loss — final values extracted by `_lastY`, which returns the last point's y or a dot placeholder), and a `MonoChart` of train/val loss with a per-run accent color. Around the grid sit a `SectionHeader`, a `Gallery` of experiment artifacts under the 03 experiment prefix, and a footer pointing at where verdicts and analysis live. Read-only; no polling, mutations, or graph writes.

`Plan` — public client component (no auth; a static section, not an HTTP route) rendering the per-workspace roadmap. Request shape: a single `workspace` prop ("01"/"02"/"03", defaulting to "03") that indexes four module-level tables — `TITLES` (header text per attempt), `SOURCES` (the on-disk docs named as source of truth in the footer), `WS_PHASES` (each phase's `id`, hardcoded status, title, and note — e.g. workspace 01's SFT→DPO→bake-off arc, 02's GRPO-null-then-best-of-k story, 03's CPT checkpoint ladder), and `WS_CHECKLIST` (done-flagged line items per attempt). Response: a `JsxElement` with two cards — PHASES, a timeline where each row shows a `StatusGlyph` for the phase status plus id/title/note, and CHECKLIST, check/circle rows styled by their done flag, footed by the workspace's source-of-truth pointer. Error cases: none at runtime — the render is fully static with no server calls, effects, or state; statuses are deliberately hardcoded to on-disk reality, so updating progress means editing this file, and an unknown `workspace` key is the only way to fault the lookups.

The DATA section for workspace 02: a read-only browser over the RL training datasets, split out from the old blended Data section (the build pipeline and add-examples remain workspace-01 features). `RlData` keeps one piece of state, `rlSource`, choosing among the `RL_SOURCES` tabs — SFT gold, GRPO reward tasks, python-to-jac conversion, synthetic, and splits — rendered as a `Segmented` control. Fetching goes through the `useRowPager` hook wired to two adapters: `_files` calls `rl_dataset_files` and `_rows` calls `rl_dataset_rows` (25 rows per page); both accept an explicit `src` override because on a source switch the freshly set `rlSource` still reads stale inside the same tick (state writes are async), so `switchSource` passes the new source straight through to the pager's loadFiles while ordinary pager clicks rely on the fresh closure. The body is header, source picker, an explanatory caption, the shared `RowBrowser` bound to the pager's files/rows/paging state and callbacks, and a source-path footer. Strictly read-only: no mutations, uploads, or graph writes.

The single action-button primitive for the studio UI. `Button` takes an `onClick` handler, `children`, a `variant` name, a `disabled` flag, and an extra `className` merged via `cn`. The `VARIANTS` map defines the three looks that cover every current use — "outline" as the default chrome action, "solid" for a section's primary action, and "ghost" for inline micro-actions like copy/delete rows — with unknown variant names falling back to outline. There is one size; width tweaks come from the caller's `className`. Disabled state layers reduced opacity and a not-allowed cursor on top of the native disabled attribute. Purely presentational; the only behavior is invoking `onClick`.

Selectable pill button used for segmented options, session pickers, file chips, and history model/stage rows. `Chip` takes an `onClick` handler, a `selected` flag, `children`, and an optional `className` merged through `cn`. Selection is communicated on two channels: the accent surface tone on the button body and the workspace accent color injected as an inline border color (only when `selected`), so the active chip stays identifiable even where tones blend; unselected chips render muted with a hover lift. Stateless and purely presentational — behavior lives entirely in the caller's `onClick`.

`CodeBlock` — public shared client component (no auth, no route) rendering a syntax-highlighted code panel with a floating label tab and a COPY button. Props (request shape): `label` for the tab text (empty falls back to an OUTPUT tag derived from `lang`, defaulting to TXT), the `code` string, and the `lang` hint. Response: a `JsxElement` — a bordered pane whose ghost `Button` copies `code` to the clipboard via the navigator API and shows COPIED for 1.2 seconds through the `copied` state, above a horizontally scrollable pre containing the highlighted spans. Highlighting is the module's real work: `_highlight` tokenizes `code` with the single `TOKEN_RE` regex (comment, double- or single-quoted string, number, word — assembled from raw-string fragments so both quote styles survive) using the JS matchAll path, since a Python regex import is unresolvable in the bundle; each match becomes a span classed "tok-com"/"tok-str"/"tok-num" or, for words, whatever `_tokClass` assigns from the keyword set `KW` (Python plus Jac keywords like walker/node/edge), the type set `TYPE`, or the builtin set `BI`, with unmatched gaps emitted as plain spans. Failure modes: none server-side (fully local); unknown tokens simply render unclassed, and clipboard access silently depends on the browser's navigator support.

The single empty/loading vocabulary for the app. `EmptyState` renders a centered `label` in micro-label styling, an optional `hint` line beneath it, and — since the app's aesthetic is text rather than spinners — a `pulse` flag that doubles as the loading state by adding the pulsing class to the label. The optional `height` fixes the container height when positive; otherwise the block sizes to its padding. Stateless and side-effect free; it takes no callbacks and renders no interactivity.

The three form primitives shared across the studio, ported from the old field component. `Field` wraps arbitrary `children` under a micro-styled `label`, giving every form row the same stacked layout. `TextInput` is a controlled text input: it renders `value`, forwards each change through `onSet` with the new string, shows `placeholder`, and applies the monospace font when `mono` is set — used for paths, ids, and numeric option fields. `Segmented` renders an exclusive choice as a row of `Chip`s over `options`, marking the chip matching `value` as selected and calling `onSet` with the clicked option. All three are stateless pass-throughs; behavior lives entirely in the callers' callbacks.

`Gallery` — shared client component (no auth beyond the session; consumes two read-only RPC endpoints) that renders repo figures verbatim: the experiments already save matplotlib PNGs under their results dirs, so this browses those directories instead of re-deriving charts. Request shape: one `prefix` prop scoping the listing to a workspace's artifacts. Server surface: `list_galleries` returns dicts with a "dir" and image "count" (filtered client-side by `prefix`, with the first match auto-opened), and `gallery_images` returns a directory's images as dicts carrying "name", "mime", base64 "b64" content, and a "note" for stubs. Response/UI: directory `Chip`s labeled by `_short` (the prefix-stripped path) plus count; an image grid where each item renders as an inline data-URI img (click sets `zoom`, opening a full-screen enlarge overlay that closes on any click) or, when "b64" is empty, a dashed stub showing the note; a source-path footer states the images are exactly as saved. Loading and error cases: `loading` shows a pulsing `EmptyState`, an empty directory list renders a NO SAVED FIGURES card naming the prefix, and both fetches are exception-swallowed so a failed endpoint degrades to the empty state rather than crashing.

Monospace log panel with newest-line-first presentation, ported from the old log-view component. `LogView` splits `text` into lines, reverses them, and renders them inside a column-reversed scrollable pre capped at `maxH` — the combination keeps the latest output pinned at the visual bottom while scrollback works naturally. Per-line coloring comes from `_lineClass`: lines containing error markers, a cross glyph, or a traceback read in full foreground; prompt lines starting with ">>>" get a slightly dimmed foreground; everything else renders muted. Empty lines are preserved as blank rows. Stateless, read-only, and side-effect free.

Single-line (optionally dual-line) chart panel used for training metrics, built on recharts with the shared chartkit chrome. `MonoChart` takes a `title` for the floating label, primary `data` and optional `secondary` series as lists of x/y dicts, a `live` flag, the stroke `accent` color, and `expY` for exponent-formatted Y ticks (the learning-rate panel). Before rendering it merges the two series into unified rows keyed by x — secondary points landing on an existing x attach as a second value, while stragglers insert in x-order so the dashed secondary line never zigzags. The primary series draws solid and dotless; the secondary draws dashed with small dots and connected nulls; `live` marks the last primary point with a `ReferenceDot` ring. An empty primary series renders a NO SIGNAL placeholder instead of an empty chart. Purely presentational with no data fetching or side effects.

The bordered-card primitive with a floating micro-label: the roughly twenty-five hand-rolled relative-border-plus-absolute-label blocks across the app collapse onto this one component. `Panel` renders its `children` inside the standard rounded, bordered card, with the `label` (omitted when empty) floating over the top border; `className` extends the card via `cn`. The `labelBg` parameter exists purely to mask the border stripe behind the label text — background-colored on page-level panels (the default), card-colored when the panel nests inside another card surface. Stateless, presentational, no side effects.

The shared dataset browser rendered by all three workspaces' DATA sections, extracted so the core, RL, and CPT views stay identical. Deliberately stateless: the parent owns every piece of state (`files`, the open `path`, `rows`, `offset`, `total`, `expanded`) plus the fetch handlers, and this module only renders and calls back — no local `has` state means none of the setter-collision gotchas apply. `RowDetail` renders one expanded row (called with a props dict): structured rows show a PROMPT block plus `CodeBlock` panes for python/jac content — DPO rows split into chosen and rejected Jac panes — while unstructured rows (CPT corpus and plain JSON) fall back to a scrollable raw-text block. `RowBrowser` is the frame: a file `Chip` strip (each showing its label and row count, selection matched against `path`, clicks routed to `onOpen`), a six-column row table (index, name, a kind badge translated through `KIND_LABEL` with unknown kinds shown verbatim, difficulty, source, preview) where clicking a row fires `onToggle` with its index and the row matching `expanded` reveals its `RowDetail`, and a pager whose PREV/NEXT `Button`s (`onPrev`/`onNext`) are enabled from `offset`/`total` arithmetic, with a range caption between them. Empty states cover no files, an empty page, and no file selected; the panel `label` defaults to a dataset-browser tag. No fetching or side effects of its own.

Document this Jac code: ```jac """SectionHeader — the top bar every section hand-rolled 10×. title/right accept elements (Train passes SubTabs as title).""" def:pub SectionHeader(title: any = None, right: any = None) -> JsxElement { return
{title}
{right}
; } ```

`SectionHeader` — shared layout component (no auth, no route, no server calls): the top bar that every section previously hand-rolled about ten times over. Request shape: two optional element props — `title`, rendered left (sections pass anything from a micro-label span to a whole SubTabs strip), and `right`, rendered on the trailing edge for status chips or counters. Response: a `JsxElement` — the standard bordered header row with both slots wrapped in aligned flex groups. No state, callbacks, or error cases; omitted props simply leave their slot empty.

Document this Jac code: ```jac """StatTile — corner-bracket stat box. Ports ui/components/shared/stat-tile.tsx.""" def:pub StatTile(label: str, value: str, sub: str, dim: bool) -> JsxElement { return
{label}
{value}
{sub and
{sub}
}
; } ```

The corner-bracket stat box used across every section's metric grids. `StatTile` renders four absolutely positioned bracket corners around a stacked readout: the micro-styled `label` on top, the large monospace `value`, and an optional `sub` caption underneath (omitted when empty). The `dim` flag drops the whole tile to reduced opacity, used for de-emphasized or unavailable metrics. Purely presentational — no state, callbacks, or side effects.

The status badge shared across the studio, which also standardizes the feed-liveness chip that the training sections used to hand-roll identically. Three lookup tables drive it: `GLYPHS` maps each status name (idle, running, done, failed, stopped, finished, plus the liveness trio live/stalled/nofeed) to its symbol, `CLASSES` maps the same names to semantic color classes — running and live pulse in the chart accent, done/finished read as success, failed as destructive with an added dashed underline, stalled as warning, the rest muted — and `LABELS` supplies display-text overrides (nofeed renders as "NO FEED"). `StatusGlyph` takes the `status` string (unknown values fall back to the idle glyph and muted tone), a `showLabel` flag controlling whether text follows the glyph, and an optional `label` that overrides the derived text (used for readouts like stall duration). Stateless, no side effects.

`SubTabs` — shared navigation component (client-side only; no auth, no server calls): the dot-separated tab strip used in section headers. Request shape (props): `tabs`, the ordered label list; `active`, the currently selected label; and `onTab`, invoked with the clicked tab's label. Response: a `JsxElement` — a bordered strip where each tab is a micro-label button, separated by dot glyphs between entries, with the tab matching `active` underlined and in full foreground while the rest render muted with a hover lift. Behavior is fully delegated: the component holds no state, so the parent must update `active` in its `onTab` handler; there are no error cases beyond a label absent from `tabs` simply never matching.

Eval-run lifecycle endpoints for the studio: detached jac eval subprocesses with history persisted in the OSP graph (each run is an `EvalRun` node attached to `root`, replacing the old SQLite table; process machinery comes from the jobs module, metric/log reading from metrics). Each run owns an artifacts dir under the results tree keyed by its `eid`, created by `eval_dir` and holding run.log, metrics.jsonl, and job.json; the exit marker in the run log is authoritative over pid liveness, and on a clean exit the last metrics row becomes the run's scores. `EvalView` is the response shape (`id`, `kind`, `model`, `adapter`, `holdout`, parsed `params` and `scores`, `pid`, `status`, `started`/`finished`, `log_tail`), produced from a node by `to_view`. Endpoints and error behavior: `create_eval` validates `kind` against `VALID_KINDS` and `holdout` against the known holdout set, resolves the model from `model_id` (must be known and on disk) or a path-sandboxed `model_path`, sanitizes the optional `adapter`, acquires the heavy-workload lock, then creates the node and spawns the job via `_start` — which builds the environment exactly like the legacy starter (eval mode, model/holdout/adapter variables, probe runs the probe script with a metrics output, idiom runs the idiom script with a similarity threshold) — returning the fresh `EvalView` or None on any validation/lock failure rather than raising. `list_evals` refreshes every run via `_refresh` (resolving finished jobs to done-with-scores, failed, or stopped — including runs whose artifacts dir vanished — and persisting the mutation) and returns them newest-first; `get_eval` returns one refreshed run with a 60-line log tail, `stop_eval` kills a running job and marks it stopped, and `delete_eval` stops if needed, deletes the graph node, and removes the artifacts dir, returning False for unknown ids. Auth is the studio session; requests are plain RPC calls, not walkers.

The studio's client entry module. Its single public component `app` returns the mounted `AppShell` — the navigation rail plus section layout — as a `JsxElement`; the runtime's entry script imports and renders this export. No parameters, state, or side effects of its own: everything (probing, routing, persistence) lives inside `AppShell` and below.

Read-only figure galleries for the studio: the experiments already render their graphs to disk as matplotlib PNGs, so this module serves those files verbatim as base64 data-URIs instead of re-deriving charts. Access is confined to `GALLERY_ROOTS` (the three experiment artifact trees) by `_allowed`, which rejects absolute paths, empty segments, and any parent-directory traversal before prefix-matching a root; `_is_img` filters by the `IMG_EXTS` suffix list and `_mime` maps suffixes to content types (PNG default). `list_galleries` walks each root under the data root and returns every directory that directly contains images as {dir, count} entries, path-sorted. `gallery_images` returns one allowlisted directory's images name-sorted as {name, mime, b64} payloads with per-request caps: at most `MAX_IMAGES` files, and any file over `MAX_BYTES` (or unreadable) is replaced by a stub entry whose note explains the skip rather than failing the request. Purely read-only — no writes, no graph mutations.

The studio's model-serving core: exactly one resident MLX model on the 48GB box, with a token stream on top. Module globals hold the residency state — `_model`, `_tokenizer`, `_current_id`, `_load_seconds` — and a threading lock (`_lock`) serializes load plus generation so a concurrent request can never swap the model mid-request; mlx imports stay inside function bodies so server boot never touches mlx. Swapping is `_unload_locked`: drop references, collect garbage, and clear the mlx cache before loading the replacement. `load_sync` is the blocking warm path: under the lock it short-circuits when the requested model is already resident (returning 0.0), otherwise unloads and loads the new weights, returning the seconds spent; `current_id` reports the resident id, and `loaded_info` returns it with a rough resident-memory estimate from the process peak RSS — there is no exact per-model byte probe, but on a single-model box RSS is dominated by the weights. `stream_chat` is the entry point for chat: holding `_lock` across the entire load-and-generate, it loads the target model if needed, yields one load frame, builds the prompt via `_build_prompt` (the tokenizer's chat template), then iterates the sampler-driven token generator yielding a token frame per step and a final done frame with counts, throughput, and timings; any failure becomes an error frame instead of crashing the generator. Cancellation is deliberately lock-free: `stream_chat` registers its generation id in `_active_gen`, `request_cancel` (called by the stop endpoint) sets `_cancel_gen` to a given or the active id, and the token loop breaks on a match — the only way to reach a generator that itself holds the lock. Side effects: model weights swapped in and out of process memory and the cross-request module state above.

The single source of chart chrome for every chart in the app, replacing the styling globals that were copy-pasted across the chart components and sections. Every color is a CSS theme token (recharts accepts var() strings for stroke/fill, resolved by the cascade), so charts re-skin with the theme switcher for free. Because module-level globals don't survive the JS module boundary, consumers call accessor functions instead: `chartColors` returns the six-token series palette and `chartColor` picks the nth entry with wraparound; `gridStroke` and `axisStroke` supply the grid and axis line tokens; `tick` returns the axis tick style (label color, small monospace type via `MONO`); and the tooltip suite — `tipContentStyle`, `tipLabelStyle`, `tipItemStyle`, and `tipCursor` — provides the props to spread onto a recharts Tooltip. All functions are pure constant accessors with no state or side effects.

The studio's entry point, joining the server surface to the client UI in one module. Its job is registration: every server endpoint and view type the client consumes — whether through an sv-import RPC stub or a raw fetch reader — must be imported here at top level or it 404s at runtime. The imports enumerate the full backend: the model registry (`ModelView`, `list_models`, `system_ram`, `loaded_model`, `warm_model`), chat persistence (`ChatView`/`MsgView` with the chat/message CRUD and `today_utc`), dataset browsing and ingest (`dataset_stats`, `dataset_files`, `dataset_rows`, `add_examples`, plus the RL browser pair), the builder pipeline (`BuilderView`, `list_builders`, `run_builder`), prompts (`list_prompts`), figure galleries (`list_galleries`, `gallery_images`), eval lifecycle (`EvalView` with `create_eval`/`list_evals`/`get_eval`/`stop_eval`/`delete_eval`), training control and run metrics (`start_training`, `stop_training`, `get_status`, `list_sessions`, `list_runs`, `get_run`, `compare_runs`), the RL results/generate endpoints (`get_rl_ladder`, `get_rl_corrected`, `rl_generate`), the CPT browser and training control (`cpt_manifest` through `get_all_cpt_status`), and the streaming chat pair (`chat_stream`, `stop_generation`) registered explicitly because the client consumes it with a raw fetch reader rather than a stub. The client block imports the global stylesheet and the frontend module, exposing the public `app` component that mounts it as the page. No logic of its own; its side effect is endpoint registration at server start.

OSP-graph persistence for chats and their messages, replacing the old SQLite tables: `Chat` nodes hang off the shared root and `Msg` nodes hang off their chat, surviving restarts, with `jid` providing the stable cross-RPC identifier. `ChatView` and `MsgView` are the wire shapes, produced by each node's `to_view`; message views carry the `role`, `content`, generating `model_id`, serialized `stats_json`, and the `pair_group` used by COMPARE mode. Timestamps come from `_now` (UTC ISO with a Z suffix), and `today_utc` returns the current UTC date string so the client can group chats by day and label the current group TODAY without touching its own clock — both being UTC keeps the grouping aligned. `_find_chat` resolves an id by scanning the root's `Chat` nodes; `_ws_of` reads a chat's `workspace` defensively so pre-workspace nodes persisted without the field resolve to the default "01". Public surface: `list_chats` returns one workspace's chats sorted most-recently-updated first, `create_chat` attaches a new node with both timestamps set, `rename_chat` retitles and touches `updated_at` (False for unknown ids), `delete_chat` removes a chat and all of its `Msg` children, `get_messages` lists a chat's messages, and `add_message` appends a message node, bumps the chat's `updated_at`, and returns the view (an empty `MsgView` when the chat is unknown). Side effects are graph mutations on the shared root.

`list_prompts` — public RPC endpoint (studio session; no additional auth) serving the prompt library. Request: no parameters. The handler resolves prompts.json relative to this module file rather than the working directory — matching the old parent-of-file behavior — so the endpoint works no matter where the server was launched from. Response: the parsed JSON file as a dict, whose "categories" list feeds the chat composer's chips and the prompt rail. Error case: any failure (missing file, unreadable content, bad JSON) is swallowed and returns {"categories": []} instead of erroring, so the client simply renders an empty library.

The RL ladder results backend: it reads the live ladder output files and pivots them into chart-ready structures for the RL RESULTS section, replacing the static weekend-only data. All paths resolve against `RL_REPO` (the repo root derived from this file's location). The core is `_pivot`: each ladder eval appends one JSONL row tagged rung/model/condition/kind, and the pivot collapses those (last write wins) into one cell per model-rung-condition — merging the generalization and memorization rows — emitting the flat cell list for the table (pass@1/pass@k/near percentages, overlap similarity, memorization pass rate, task count, and per-family breakdowns), a rung-indexed curve keyed by model-condition line names ordered by `RUNG_ORDER`, and the sorted key/family lists. Curves are densified: every rung row carries every series key with None where that series had no eval, so the client can render explicit N/A markers instead of silently dropping series. `get_rl_ladder` assembles the primary run (path overridable via the JAC_RL_RESULTS environment variable), the sg-holdout run, and the 84-task rerun into one payload; `get_rl_corrected` serves the pre-assembled corrected-results summary JSON, always merging over an empty shape that carries every key the client dereferences unguarded, with a note on unreadable files. `rl_generate` is the deployable best-of-k artifact: after checking the fused SFT model at `GEN_MODEL` exists and claiming the single heavy-workload slot (returning ok-false with the busy holder otherwise), it runs the generation script via subprocess with the model and `k` in the environment (15-minute timeout), parses the output into a note and the generated Jac, flags whether the compiler verified it, and always releases the heavy slot. Side effects: the generation subprocess and heavy-lock file; everything else is read-only.

Read-only training-run metrics endpoints for the Train section's MONITOR and HISTORY views; all parsing is delegated to the metrics module and liveness to the jobs module, this file only assembles responses. Internals: `_run_dir` locates a run under the results tree, `_f`/`_i` coerce untyped dict values, `_is_running` reports whether either the SFT or DPO job file resolves to a running status, `_pick_idiom` chooses the best idiom-metrics file for a run/mode (DPO artifacts nest under a subdirectory; function holdout preferred over graph; only files whose last row carries a similarity score qualify), and `_idiom_obj` normalizes an idiom summary into the has/avg-sim/idiomatic/python-shaped/runs/total shape. The workhorse `_get_run_metrics` builds the full RunMetrics dict for one run and mode: parsed train/val/lr/tps series and last iteration from the train log, the accuracy curve read from the SFT metrics file, the idiom similarity series and summary with a human `idiom_label`, both `func_idiom` and `graph_idiom` holdout objects, a live `running` flag from the mode's job file, a `found` flag keyed on the log's existence, and a 40-line log tail. Public endpoints: `list_runs` walks the results dir (skipping non-run directories in the exclusion list) and summarizes each run's SFT/DPO presence, completed stages, and liveness; `get_run` validates `name` (shell-safe) and `mode` (sft or dpo, raising ValueError otherwise) and returns the full metrics; `compare_runs` collects every found run for a mode, merges their train/val/accuracy series into overlay rows via the metrics module's x-merge, and adds per-run headline numbers (final pass, last loss via `_last_y`, idiom stats, last iteration). No mutations anywhere — strictly filesystem reads.

Training job control endpoints — public RPC functions (studio session; no per-user auth) driving detached SFT/DPO runs, with process lifecycle in the jobs module, log parsing in metrics, and path/registry resolution in models. Artifact layout per run: a per-mode job JSON and run log under the run's results directory, plus the train log (nested under a dpo subdirectory for DPO), located by `_job_file`, `_run_log`, and `_train_log`. `_build_status` is the shared response shape: with no job record it reports finished-or-idle from the train log's existence with the last iteration and a 40-line log tail; with one it passes through the live status, pid, `run_id`, and start time, plus an optional message. `start_training` validates the shell-safe `name` (rejecting reserved results directories), the sft/dpo `mode`, and — for SFT — a path-safe `model_id`, raising ValueError on each; it then short-circuits with "already running", claims the single heavy-workload slot (returning a busy message naming the holder on contention), filters `opts` to the mode's allowlisted environment keys (`SFT_KEYS`/`DPO_KEYS`, unknown keys reported back as ignored rather than erroring), prepends the venv to PATH, and launches the mode's run script detached from the data root, returning the fresh status. `stop_training` SIGTERMs the job's process group, but when a `run_id` is supplied and a newer run now owns the slot it stops nothing and says the run was superseded. `get_status` is the 2.5-second poll target, and `list_sessions` enumerates every SFT/DPO session across run directories — including finished ones with only a train log — reporting status (idle job records normalize to finished), last iteration, start time, and a display label. Side effects: detached training subprocesses and their job/log files.

A standalone build script (all logic in the top-level entry block, run via jac run from the repo root) that packages the DPO preference pairs into the train/valid splits the third-party mlx-lm-lora trainer consumes — the installed mlx-lm has no native DPO. It reads the pair file named by `SRC`, drops blank lines, strips each record down to exactly the prompt/chosen/rejected keys the trainer's DPO dataset expects (discarding the meta provenance; the trainer wraps prompt as the user turn and the two completions as assistant turns via the chat template), and writes train.jsonl and valid.jsonl under `OUT_DIR`. The split is a deterministic stride: every `VALID_EVERY`-th pair goes to valid (about 10%), so the validation set stratifies across the whole pool instead of clustering. A missing source file prints a pointer to the upstream conversion step instead of failing; on success it prints the split sizes. Side effects: creates the output directory and overwrites both split files.

Builds the balanced SFT training manifest that de-skews idiomatic versus transpile data: the raw pool runs about 1:14 idiomatic-to-transpile, which would teach Python-shaped Jac. Reading the idiomatic core from `IDIOMATIC` and the transpile tier from `TRANSPILE` via the blank-line-filtering `read_lines` helper, the entry block keeps ALL idiomatic examples and caps the transpile contribution at `RATIO` times the idiomatic count — taking the whole tier when it already fits, otherwise stride-sampling deterministically across it so the sample spans the file rather than truncating it. The combined manifest is written to `OUT` (idiomatic first, then the sample); the finetune trains on this file while the full transpile file is retained untouched. Prints the counts and the achieved ratio. Run from the repo root as a standalone jac script; side effects are the output file write and directory creation.

Companion packaging script to the manifest builder: it converts the balanced SFT manifest into the train/valid files mlx-lm trains on. The entry block reads the manifest at `SRC` (skipping blank lines), strips each record to a plain messages-only object — the mlx-lm chat format, dropping the meta provenance — and writes train.jsonl and valid.jsonl under `OUT_DIR`. Splitting is a deterministic stride, sending every `VALID_EVERY`-th record (about 10%) to valid so validation stratifies across the interleaved idiomatic-then-transpile ordering instead of concentrating one tier. A missing manifest prints a pointer to run the manifest builder first; success prints the split sizes. Run standalone from the repo root; side effects are the output directory creation and the two overwritten split files.

Zero-dependency ASCII training dashboard: a standalone jac script that renders terminal charts from training artifacts, no matplotlib required — the probe runner re-executes it on a timer for a live view. `parse_train` scans the mlx trainer log line by line, extracting per-iteration series via the `_num` regex helper: train and val loss, learning rate, tokens/sec, iterations/sec, cumulative trained tokens, and peak memory, each as [iteration, value] pairs (missing files yield empty series). Rendering is `render`, which prints a labelled section with the series min/max and the last twelve points, each drawn as a proportional hash-bar scaled by `bar` between the observed bounds; empty series print a no-data placeholder. The entry block resolves the log and metrics paths from the JAC_TRAIN_LOG and JAC_METRICS environment variables (with defaults under the results dir), renders all seven training series, then reads the per-checkpoint metrics JSONL — skipping blank or partial lines — to chart the holdout test-pass learning curve per checkpoint step. Read-only: output is entirely terminal printing.

Decontamination utilities that guard the eval holdout against near-duplicates of the training set. `extract_python` pulls the Python source out of a training record's first user message (empty when no python fence is present). `shingles` turns code into overlapping `n`-token strings (default 14) using `code_tokens` from the dedup module. `build_training_shingles` reads every JSONL file in `paths` and accumulates the shingle set of all training Python into one `dict`. `is_contaminated` shingles a candidate's `py` source and returns True when the fraction of its shingles found in `train` reaches `threshold` (default 0.5). Pure library module: no entry point and no graph state; holdout builders import these to filter candidates.

Runs a decontamination audit over the conversion eval holdout. Builds the training 14-gram shingle set from the files listed in `TRAIN` via `build_training_shingles`, then reads each JSONL record from `HOLDOUT`, extracts its `python` field, and flags it with `is_contaminated`. Prints the shingle count, the `func_name` of every contaminated task, and a final clean/contaminated summary from the `total` and `contam` counters. Takes no parameters and returns nothing; it only reads files and writes to stdout, with no graph side effects.

Within-candidate dedup helpers based on ROUGE-L similarity. `code_tokens` strips `#` comments and splits code into whitespace tokens. `lcs_len` computes the longest-common-subsequence length of token lists `a` and `b` with a rolling DP row. `rouge_l` returns the ROUGE-L F1 of two code strings (0.0 when either side tokenizes to nothing). `dedup_examples` walks `examples` in order, extracts each assistant Jac body, drops any example whose `rouge_l` against an already-kept body reaches `threshold` (default 0.6), and returns a tuple of the kept examples and the `removed` count. All pure functions; no file or graph side effects.

Append-only ingest of agent-authored DPO pairs for the conversion dataset. The entry block reads a staged batch JSON named by the `JAC_BATCH` env var and refuses to re-run when a receipt for its `batch_id` already exists under `RECEIPT_DIR`. Each pair is gated: the Python prompt must not be `is_contaminated` against the holdout shingles (`holdout_shingles` builds them from `HOLDOUT_PATHS`); both the `chosen_jac` and `rejected_jac` must pass the parse-only `parses` gate (which shells out to a jac parse check in a temp dir); and `rouge_l` between chosen and rejected must stay below `CONTRAST_MAX` (0.85) so the pair carries real contrast. Accepted pairs are appended to `DPO_PATH` via `append_jsonl` with meta including `rejected_style`, recipe, and `batch_id`; finally a receipt with the accepted/rejected tallies and accept rate is written, making ingestion idempotent.

Generates conversion DPO pairs by pairing each idiomatic example in `SFT_PATH` against a mechanical transpile of the same Python. For each stored record the entry block extracts the Python prompt with `extract_python` and the idiomatic Jac (minus its demo entry block) with `extract_idiomatic`, then builds the rejected side via `transpile` plus `sanitize_transpile`; pairs whose transpile is empty or fails the parse-only `compiles` gate are skipped. Side effects: truncates and rewrites `DPO_PATH`, appending one pair per surviving record through `append_jsonl` with meta copied from the source example, then prints the `made` and `skipped` counts. No graph state is touched.

Behavioral eval harness that scores a model on the conversion holdout. The entry block reads the holdout at `HOLDOUT` (overridable via env `JAC_HOLDOUT`) and picks a generation mode with `eval_mode`: a mechanical transpile stand-in, or an mlx model loaded once by `load_model` (adapter from `JAC_EVAL_ADAPTER`). Per task it generates Jac (`gen_mlx` streams from the loaded model and records token counts), extracts the code block with `extract_jac`, resolves the function name with `detect_func`, wraps it with the recorded `test_cases` into a runnable program via `build_program`, and executes it through `run_jac`, comparing stdout to the expected outputs. Prints run rate, test pass rate, total generation tokens, average tokens/sec, and tokens-to-correct; when `JAC_EVAL_METRICS_OUT` is set it appends a metrics row (step from `JAC_EVAL_STEP`) to that file. Side effects are stdout and the optional metrics file only.

Builds the graph-shaped eval holdout file. `make_prompt` wraps a Python function in the standard convert-to-Jac instruction. The entry block loads the validated task list from `TASKS` and, when present, rewrites `OUT_PATH` from scratch (an idempotent fresh write), emitting one JSONL record per task with keys `func_name`, `python`, `prompt`, `test_cases`, and `source` (set to the `SOURCE` constant), where the prompt is rendered by `make_prompt` over the task's `py` field. If the task file is missing it prints a pointer to run the authoring harness first. Entry point: run the file directly; no graph state is involved.

Appends the graph-tier idiomatic conversion seeds to the SFT dataset. Reads the validated task list at `TASKS`; for each task it renders a self-running program (`jac_full`: the stored `jac` body plus a `demo` entry block printing the function applied to the first case's input), re-validates it through `run_jac`, and requires exit 0 with stdout equal to the case's `expected` output. Passing tasks are converted with `make_sft_example` (carrying the task's `difficulty`) and appended to `SFT_PATH` via `append_jsonl`. Prints per-task failures plus the final `written` and `failed` counts. Side effects: appends JSONL lines to `SFT_PATH`; no persistent graph is touched.

Idiom-quality judge layered on the conversion holdout: it splits behaviorally correct model outputs into idiomatic versus Python-shaped. Generation mirrors the behavioral probe — `eval_mode` selects the mode, `load_model` and `gen_mlx` drive an mlx model loaded once, `extract_jac` pulls the code block, and `detect_func` + `build_program` + `run_jac` verify each output against the task's `test_cases`. For outputs that run correctly, the entry block computes `rouge_l` similarity against the mechanical baseline (`transpile` + `sanitize_transpile`) and counts Jac-native constructs with `idiom_features` over the `IDIOM_MARKERS` list; outputs at or above `sim_thresh` (env `JAC_IDIOM_SIM`, default 0.7) land in the `python_shaped` bucket, below it in `idiomatic`. Prints the split with average similarity and idiom-construct counts, and appends a metrics row to the file named by `JAC_IDIOM_OUT` when set. Entry point: run directly with the eval env vars; the holdout path defaults to `HOLDOUT` and is overridable via `JAC_HOLDOUT`.

Central quality gate that ingests one staged SFT batch into the conversion dataset. The entry block loads the batch JSON named by env `JAC_BATCH` and refuses re-ingestion when a receipt already exists in `RECEIPT_DIR`. Each example is first decontamination-checked (`is_contaminated` against `holdout_shingles` built from `HOLDOUT_PATHS`), then vetted by `check_example`: every case must run in Jac (`run_jac` over `jac_with_demo` renderings) and cross-check in Python (`run_python`, which calls the example's declared `name` rather than parsing the source), and the assembled `jac_full` must stay below the ROUGE-L dedup threshold against both `existing` bodies and `batch_kept` earlier acceptances — `DEDUP_THRESHOLD` (0.6) normally, `GRAPH_DEDUP_THRESHOLD` (0.95) for the `graph_osp` category. Accepted examples are enriched with subcategory/batch metadata and appended to `SFT_PATH` via `make_sft_example` + `append_jsonl`; a receipt with accepted/rejected lists and the accept rate is then written. Side effects: appends to `SFT_PATH`, writes the receipt, prints a summary.

Append-only ingestion of new graph eval-holdout tasks from a staged batch. The entry block reads the batch JSON named by env `JAC_BATCH`, refusing to re-run when a receipt for its `batch_id` exists under `RECEIPT_DIR`. Gates per task: its `name` must not already be in the `taken` set from `HOLDOUT_PATH`; its Python must not be `is_contaminated` against the training shingles built from `TRAIN_PATHS`; and on every case both the Python (via `run_python`) and the stripped `jac_reference` (executed with `run_jac` plus a generated demo entry) must reproduce the recorded output — the reference proves solvability but is never stored. Accepted tasks are appended to `HOLDOUT_PATH` as records with `func_name`, `python`, `prompt`, `test_cases`, and `source`, and a receipt with the accepted and `rejected` lists plus accept rate is written. The holdout file is never truncated.

Corpus miner that harvests self-contained, runnable Python functions for the conversion pipeline. `fetch_rows` pages rows from the HuggingFace datasets-server for `DATASET` via curl. `first_func` slices out the first top-level function of a row's output; `is_clean` rejects anything using banned constructs (`BANNED`), imports outside `ALLOWED_IMPORTS`, no return statement, or the wrong length. `try_run` then executes the candidate, requires exactly one parameter, and probes it against the fixed `INPUTS` pool until it yields a printable value, recording the working input/output pair. `mine` chains these stages into a kept list of records (`func_name`, `python`, `call_input`, `expected_output`, `source`), and `write_pool` writes them as JSONL to `POOL_PATH`. Entry point: the `with entry` block mines 400 rows for up to 40 functions, persists the pool, and prints a sample of mined names.

Renders training-run graphs as PNG files with matplotlib. `_num` extracts one float from a log `line` by regex `pattern` (returning -1.0 on no match). `parse_train` scans the training log at `path` for iteration lines and collects series for train loss, val loss, learning rate, tokens/sec, iterations/sec, trained tokens, and peak memory. `plot_one` renders a single [iteration, value] series (`points`) to `outpath` with the given `title` and `ylabel`, silently skipping empty series. The entry block reads paths from env (`JAC_TRAIN_LOG`, `JAC_METRICS`, `JAC_PLOT_DIR`), plots every parsed series, then parses the per-checkpoint metrics JSONL into a holdout learning curve. Side effects: writes PNG files into the plot directory and prints each written path; no graph state.

Volume-tier generator that mines Python from an online corpus and keeps only behaviorally-verified mechanical transpiles. `build_program` wraps a transpiled function (`jac_fn`) and its test `inputs` into a runnable program; `difficulty_of` labels short transpiles atomic and longer ones idiomatic. The entry block truncates `OUT_PATH`, then pages the corpus via `fetch_page` up to `SCAN_CAP`: candidates pass `first_func` and `is_clean`, are deduped on their `normalize` form, get behavioral cases from `py_cases`, are transpiled with `transpile`, and must reproduce the expected outputs under `run_jac` before `make_sft_example` + `append_jsonl` store them. Stops at `TARGET` kept examples (or after repeated empty pages) and prints running and final statistics including the `tp_fail` and `behave_fail` counters.

Independent integrity audit for the stored conversion datasets. `audit_file` walks one JSONL file line by line, optionally sampling every Nth record (`SAMPLE_EVERY`, overridable via env `JAC_SAMPLE_EVERY`), re-runs each record through `revalidate_example`, and returns a `dict` of `checked` and `failed` counts while printing each failure with its line number. The entry block iterates the dataset paths in `FILES`, aggregates per-file and total tallies, and prints them. Entry point: run the file directly; it only reads the dataset files and writes to stdout — nothing on disk or in a graph is modified.

Splits the conversion RL task file into train and holdout partitions with a simple stride. Reads all non-blank lines of the tasks JSONL, sends every fourth record to `hold` and the rest to `train`, writes the two lists to the holdout and train JSONL files, and prints the counts. Takes no parameters; side effects are the two files written under the rl_conv dataset directory and one summary line on stdout. No graph state is involved.

Builds Python-to-Jac conversion tasks by reusing the existing hole-fill task bank. The entry block first loads the hole-fill records, mapping each task id to its raw answer JSON string in `ans_by_id` so grading metadata is reused verbatim. It then iterates the conversion Python sidecar files; for each sidecar whose id (`tid`) has both a matching answer and a template at `tmpl_path`, it renders the template with its hole replaced by a TODO comment (`jac_todo`) and composes a `prompt` showing the Python function plus the incomplete Jac file. Each record with `prompt` and `answer` keys is collected into `out` and written to the rl_conv tasks JSONL; unmatched sidecars are counted in `skipped` and reported alongside `built`. Entry point: run directly after the hole-fill task builder has produced the templates (it exits early if the tasks file is missing).

Partitions the RL task corpus into a sound holdout / trainpool / valid split. Helpers: `meta_of` decodes a task line's answer metadata, `family_of` and `source_of` derive its id-prefix family and origin file, and `refbody_of` loads its gold reference body. The entry block greedily holds out whole source files (capped near half the `n_hold` target, always picking the eligible file adding the most new families), decontaminates the holdout by dropping any task whose reference body is difflib-similar at or above `thresh` to a train body, round-robin interleaves the remaining pool by family so every prefix slice is balanced, and carves `valid` from the trainpool tail so it never overlaps the holdout. Writes the holdout, trainpool, train, and valid JSONL files via `dump` and prints a report with WARN guards for a too-small or single-family holdout. Env knobs: `JAC_RL_HOLDOUT_N`, `JAC_RL_VALID_N`, `JAC_RL_DECONTAM`.

Builds a supervised warm-start SFT set from the gold reference bodies of the RL train tasks. Reads the task file named by env `JAC_RL_TRAIN` (defaulting to the rl train split); for each task it looks up the reference-body sidecar by task id and, when present, emits a chat pair whose user turn is the task `prompt` and whose assistant turn is the `gold` body wrapped in a jac code fence, counting missing sidecars in `skipped`. The pairs are then split roughly 5:1 into `train` and `valid` (with a fallback so `valid` is never empty) and written as messages-format JSONL under the rft directory. Holdout tasks are never read, so the eval set stays unseen. Side effects: creates the rft directory, writes the two JSONL files, and prints a summary.

Task builder that turns authored RL driver files into GRPO records. `run_jac` executes a driver in a temp working dir (fresh persistence per run) and is the behavioral gate; `parse_hole` locates the sentinel-marked body and returns its id, instruction, indentation, and line span; `replace_region` splices replacement lines into the file; `sg_bucket` maps a social-graph task id into one of four feature buckets so the oversized source can be subdivided (opt-in via env `JAC_RL_SG_BUCKETS`). The entry block truncates `tasks_path`, then per driver: verifies it runs clean and deterministically (two identical runs), captures the ground-truth stdout as `expected_output`, writes a `template` with the body replaced by the `__HOLE__` sentinel, writes the reference-body sidecar (`ref_body`), and appends a record with `prompt` and `answer` fields whose prompt embeds a TODO-marked view (`prompt_view`) of the file. Prints the `built` and `failed` totals. Entry point: run directly; the whole task set is rebuilt each time.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the `deliver` ability of the `explore_graph` walker. On `Root` exit the ability appends a completion line (built from the length of `self.nodes`) to `self.log`, then reports a `GraphSnapshot` assembled from the walker's `nodes`, `edges`, `path`, and `log` fields. The only mutations are to the walker's own state and its report stream; the graph itself is untouched. The `with entry` block spawns the walker on `root` pre-filled with three fixed `GraphNodeView` entries and a fixed log, then prints the joined log, which is byte-stable every run.

RL driver modeling the guestbook graph walk with the `walk_day` ability as the regeneration target. The graph is root to `Day` to `Visitor`, wired by `OnDay` and `Signed` edges; `GraphNodeView` and `GraphSnapshot` are the plain view objects the walk accumulates. The `explore_graph` walker relates its four abilities in sequence: `run` (on `Root` entry) seeds `rid`, records the root view, and visits the days; `walk_day` (the marked hole) records each `Day` as a view keyed by its `date`, appends the root-to-day edge, the path step, and a log line, then descends to that day's visitors; `walk` records each `Visitor` by `name` with its parent day; and `deliver` (on `Root` exit) appends the completion line and reports the final `GraphSnapshot`. Entry point: the `with entry` block builds one fixed day with two visitors, spawns the walker on `root`, and prints deterministic counts, kinds, labels, and log.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the `deliver` ability of the `get_guestbook` walker. On `Root` exit it sorts `self.results` in place by each entry's `created_at` field in descending order — using a lambda whose parameter is typed as `GuestEntry` — and reports the first 50 entries. Side effects are limited to reordering the walker's own `results` list and emitting the report; no graph nodes or edges are touched. The `with entry` block seeds the walker with three fixed `GuestEntry` literals and prints the names joined by commas, always yielding the recency order carol,bob,alice.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the `descend` ability of the `get_guestbook` walker. On `Day` entry the ability visits every `Visitor` node one hop out from `here`, enqueueing the day's visitors so the scaffold abilities can collect them: `run` enters the days from `Root`, `gather` appends each visitor's `name` to `self.names`, and `done` sorts the list on exit. `descend` itself only schedules traversal — it mutates nothing. The `with entry` block idempotently attaches a fixed graph (one `Day` with two visitors via `OnDay` and `Signed` edges) only when the persisted `root` has no `Day` yet, then spawns the walker and prints the sorted, comma-joined names.

RL driver modeling the guestbook read path with the `gather` ability as the regeneration target. `Day` and `Visitor` nodes hang off `root` via `OnDay` and `Signed` edges, and `Visitor` carries a `to_view` method producing a `GuestEntry` value object. The `get_guestbook` walker traverses in one pass: `run` visits the days from `Root`, `descend` fans into each day's visitors, `gather` (the marked hole) appends `here.to_view()` to `self.results`, and `deliver` sorts the collected entries by `created_at` descending and reports the top 50. Entry point: the `with entry` block builds one fixed day with three fixed-timestamp visitors, spawns the walker, and prints the deterministic count, recency-ordered names and messages, and sorted names.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the `sign` ability of the `sign_guestbook` walker. `run` (on `Root` entry) bails on a blank `message`, then visits today's `Day` node, creating it via an `OnDay` edge (granted `ConnectPerm`) on the day's first signature. The marked `sign` ability, on `Day` entry, hangs a new `Visitor` off `here` through a `Signed` edge — `name` stripped and capped at 40 chars with an anonymous fallback, `message` stripped and capped at 200 chars, `created_at` a fixed literal — grants the fresh node `ReadPerm`, and reports its `to_view()` projection. Side effects: adds one `Visitor` node and one `Signed` edge to the persisted day per invocation. The `with entry` block signs twice (named and anonymous) and prints the entry fields plus day and visitor counts.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the `act` ability of the `like_tweet` walker, which subclasses `find_tweet` (the base resolves the caller's `actor` username and navigates to the target `Tweet` by its `jid`). On `Tweet` entry, and only when the node matches `self.tweet_id`, `act` toggles `self.actor` in `here.likes`: removing it reports a liked-False result with the updated list, adding it reports liked-True — in both branches `here.likes` is reassigned to a fresh list rather than mutated in place, and the walker disengages after reporting. Side effect: the `likes` field of the persisted `Tweet` node changes on each call. The `with entry` block builds one profile and tweet, spawns the walker twice, and prints the like-then-unlike results.

RL driver modeling hashtag trending over a social graph, with the `tally` ability as the regeneration target. `Profile` and `Tweet` nodes are wired under `root` (a `Post` edge type is declared), and `TrendingTag` is the plain result object. The `get_trending` walker fans out in `run` across every root returned by `allroots` to each profile's tweets; `tally` (the marked hole) dedupes tweets by `jid` via `self.seen`, then scans `here.content` for hashtag words, normalising each with lowercasing and punctuation right-strip and incrementing `self.counts`; `deliver` converts the counts into `TrendingTag` objects sorted by descending `count` and reports the top 8. Entry point: the `with entry` block builds one profile with three fixed tweets, spawns the walker, and prints the deterministic tag/count list.

Deterministic RL driver isolating a source-type sniffing heuristic. `analyse_text` returns a `bool`: True when the `text` argument's shebang line matches the Python interpreter pattern via Pygments' `shebang_matches` helper, or when the literal substring "import " occurs within the first 1000 characters. Pure predicate — no state, IO, or graph effects. The `with entry` block probes three fixed strings (an import line, a python3 shebang, and a walker snippet) and prints the boolean results.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the failure-tail formatter from the benchmark capture runner. `_output_tail` strips leading and trailing whitespace from `out`, splits it into lines, and returns the last eight lines rejoined with newlines — a pure `str` transformation with no side effects. The `with entry` block runs it over four fixed cases (padded multi-line, single-line, empty, and a 12-line block) and prints each tail behind a separator, producing byte-identical output every run.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the blank-file payload builder. `_blank` returns a `dict` describing an empty file result: the path key set to `rel`, the error key set to `err`, and fixed defaults — empty lang, html, and raw strings, a lines count of 0, and truncated False. Pure construction, no side effects. The `with entry` block builds payloads for three fixed path/error pairs and prints a pipe-joined projection of the fields.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the status-to-marker mapping used in capture log lines. `_status_mark` maps the `status` string to a fixed four-character label: "ok  " (with two trailing spaces) for ok, "skip" for skip, and "FAIL" for anything else — a single pure conditional expression with no side effects. The `with entry` block prints the bracketed marker for six fixed inputs, including case-mismatched and empty strings that fall through to "FAIL".

Deterministic RL driver isolating the ok-counting step of the capture summary. `count_ok` takes `results`, a `list` of result dicts, and returns how many have a status value equal to ok, computed as the `len` of a filtering list comprehension. Pure function, no mutation of its input. The `with entry` block counts a fixed four-element result list with mixed statuses and prints 2 every run.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the `record` method of the `CaptureRunner` object. `record` appends a `dict` with step, status, and detail keys (from the `name`, `status`, and `detail` arguments) to `self.results`, derives the four-character `mark` ("ok  ", "skip", or "FAIL") from `status`, and prints the formatted log line. Side effects: grows the runner's `results` list and writes one stdout line per call; returns `None`. The `with entry` block records three fixed triples covering all three branches and prints a sorted JSON projection of the accumulated results.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the exit-code decision from the capture summary. `_summary_code` counts the entries of `results` whose status is ok into `oks` and returns 0 when at least one step succeeded, otherwise 1. Pure function over its argument, no side effects. The `with entry` block evaluates four fixed result lists — empty, no-ok, one-ok, and multi-ok — and prints the resulting codes.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the current-matrix selector from the raylib shim. `_cur` inspects `sh.mode` and returns `sh.proj` when the mode equals 0x1701 (projection mode), otherwise `sh.mv` — a single pure conditional with no mutation. `Shim` is the minimal inlined `obj` holding the `proj` and `mv` matrix lists and the `mode` field. The `with entry` block builds one shim per branch and prints the selected matrices.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the handle-shortening helper from the littlex frontend. `display_username` returns the part of `profileUsername` before the first at-sign when the string contains one, otherwise the string unchanged — pure splitting, no side effects. The `with entry` block maps five fixed samples (including an empty string and a multi-at handle) and prints a single joined projection line.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the feed search filter. `_search_filter` lowercases and strips `query` into `q`, then returns the members of `contents` whose lowercased form contains `q` as a substring — a pure case-insensitive filter where an empty query matches everything. No side effects. The `with entry` block filters a fixed four-item list with four queries (padded uppercase, plain, missing, and empty) and prints each resulting list.

RL driver modeling the shooter's fire action with the `fire` body as the regeneration target. Fixed globs supply the camera (`yaw`, `pitch`) and player position (`px`, `py`, `pz`); `DEG2RAD` converts degrees to radians. `jcos` is a range-reduced Taylor-series cosine and `jsin` derives sine from it, so the aim math is deterministic without a math library. `fire` converts yaw and pitch to radians, computes the aim direction, and scans `bullets` (a pool of `Bullet` objects) for the first slot whose `life` is spent, placing it at the player position, setting its velocity to the aim direction times a fixed speed of 40.0, resetting `life` to 2.0, and returning immediately; live bullets are skipped. Entry point: the `with entry` block fires into a two-bullet pool where only index 1 is dead and prints its rounded state.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the benchmark table-row formatter. `_fmt_row` renders one padded row: when `d` is `None` it emits the `label` left-justified with three right-justified n/a columns; otherwise it formats `d.avg` and `d.max` through the `_one_dp` one-decimal helper and right-justifies them along with `d.frames`. `BenchResult` is the minimal result `obj`, and `_one_dp` is provided un-holed. Pure string padding, no side effects. The `with entry` block prints two populated rows and one `None` row.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the f-string highlighting rules from the Pygments-based lexer. `fstring_rules` returns a fixed `list` of regex rule tuples for an f-string body: a closing brace tagged `String.Interpol`, an opening brace tagged `String.Interpol` that also transitions into the nested expression state, a run of ordinary characters tagged with the caller's `ttype`, and a single quote-or-backslash rule also tagged `ttype`. Pure constant construction from raw-string fragments; no side effects. The `with entry` block builds the rules for `String.Double` and prints the rule count plus each regex pattern.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the path normalization at the top of the source browser's file lookup. `_normalize_rel` strips any leading forward slashes from `rel` and converts every backslash to a forward slash, returning the cleaned repo-relative path — pure string work, no side effects. The `with entry` block normalizes six fixed inputs (leading slash, double slash, Windows-style, already-clean, UNC-like, and empty) and prints each mapping.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the size-cap step of the source browser's file reader. `_truncate_data` sets `truncated` when the length of `data` exceeds `max_bytes`; if so it cuts the data to the cap and appends a fixed truncation notice, then strips trailing newlines and returns the data/flag tuple. Pure transformation of its arguments, no side effects. The `with entry` block runs four fixed cases — under the cap, over it, trailing newlines, and exactly at it — and prints each flag with the repr'd result.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the path-exclusion predicate of the source indexer. `_should_skip` returns True when `rel` should be excluded: any path containing a pycache component, a dot-prefixed basename, or a lowercased extension (`ext`, via `os.path.splitext`) belonging to the `_BINARY_EXTS` glob set; otherwise False. Pure string tests and `set` membership. The `with entry` block classifies seven fixed paths — covering each exclusion rule plus keepers — and prints the verdicts.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the hashtag normalization used by the trending tally. `_norm_tag` lowercases `word` and right-strips the trailing punctuation characters period, comma, bang, question mark, semicolon, and colon — a pure two-step string transform with no side effects. The `with entry` block normalizes five fixed hashtag tokens and prints each result.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the staged raylib shared-library filename test. `_is_lib` returns a `bool`: when `osname` is Darwin the filename `fn` must both start with libraylib and end with .dylib; on any other OS it must start with libraylib.so. Pure prefix/suffix checks, no side effects. The `with entry` block evaluates five fixed filename/OS pairs across both branches and prints the results.

RL driver packaging the range-reduced Taylor cosine as a standalone unit. `jcos` first folds its angle `a` into the [-pi, pi] interval by repeatedly adding or subtracting `twopi`, then evaluates a 7-term even-power Taylor series (through the `x12` term) to approximate cosine — pure float arithmetic with no math-library dependency, so results are identical every run. The marked hole is the entire function body. Entry point: the `with entry` block sweeps seven fixed angles (including both pi boundaries and a full-turn wrap) and prints each value rounded to 6 decimal places.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the sine helper built on the Taylor cosine. `jsin` returns `jcos` applied to `a` minus the quarter-turn constant 1.5707963267948796, turning the inlined range-reduced cosine into a sine — pure arithmetic, no side effects. `jcos` is provided verbatim outside the hole. The `with entry` block evaluates six fixed angles and prints each result rounded to 6 decimal places.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the DOM-to-raylib key mapping. `_keymap` builds a fixed `dict` `m` from DOM key-code strings (the WASD keys, Space, Tab, and the four arrow codes) to raylib integer keycodes, and returns the entry for `code`, defaulting to 0 for unknown codes. Pure lookup, no side effects. The `with entry` block maps four fixed codes — one of them unknown — and prints the space-joined keycodes.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the 31-bit LCG step. `rand01` declares the module-level `rng` glob as global, advances it with the classic multiplier-and-increment recurrence modulo 2147483648, and returns the new state divided by 2147483648.0 as a `float` in the [0, 1) range. Side effect: each call mutates the `rng` glob, making the sequence reproducible from the fixed seed. The `with entry` block draws six values and prints them rounded to 9 decimal places, byte-stable every run.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the per-file metadata record built by the source browser's listing. `_file_meta` returns a `dict` with the path key set to `rel`, the name from `os.path.basename`, the dir from `os.path.dirname`, the lang from the inlined `_lang_label` helper (backed by the `_LANG` table), and the size set to the caller-supplied `size`. Pure construction; no filesystem access or mutation. The `with entry` block builds records for four fixed path/size pairs and prints a pipe-joined projection of each.

Deterministic RL driver isolating the benchmark logger's line prefixer. `_log` prints `msg` prefixed with the two greater-than characters and a space using the built-in `print`, returning `None` — its only side effect is the single stdout line per call. The `with entry` block logs two fixed messages, producing identical output every run.

with entry block exercises it on fixed inputs and prints a deterministic projection
(floats rounded to 6 dp).

Position 0 is 2*n/(r-l); position 5 is 2*n/(t-b); position 8 is (r+l)/(r-l); position 9 is (t+b)/(t-b); position 10 is -(f+n)/(f-n); position 11 is -1.0; position 14 is -2*f*n/(f-n). All other positions are 0.0."

    ];

with entry {

Assumes `nums` is non-empty. Pure function with no side effects on the graph; the entry block prints the minimum of five sample lists covering negatives, a singleton, and an all-equal list.

Returns the most frequent whitespace-separated word of a string, breaking ties by earliest appearance. `most_common_word` splits `s`, tallies occurrences in the `counts` `dict` while recording each word's first appearance in `order`, then scans `order` keeping `best`; because only a strictly greater count replaces `best`, a tie is won by the word seen first. Assumes `s` contains at least one word and returns it as a `str`. No side effects on the graph; the entry block prints the winner for four sample phrases.

Reverses the order of the words in a string. `reverse_words` splits `s` on whitespace, reverses the word list with a slice, and joins the words back with single spaces, returning the resulting `str`. Any run of whitespace in the input therefore collapses to one space, and a single word comes back unchanged. No side effects on the graph; the entry block prints the reversal of four sample strings.

Rounds a non-negative `float` to two decimal places without using the round() builtin. `round2` scales `x` by 100.0, adds 0.5, truncates through `int`, and divides back by 100.0, returning the `float`. The add-then-truncate trick rounds halves upward and is only correct for non-negative inputs (a negative `x` would truncate toward zero the wrong way). No side effects on the graph; the entry block prints five sample roundings, e.g. 9.999 becoming 10.0.

Run-length encodes a string. `run_length_encode` returns the empty string for empty input, otherwise it walks `s` tracking the current run character in `prev` and its length in `count`; when the character changes it flushes the pair into `result` as the character immediately followed by its count in digits, and the final run is flushed after the loop ("aaab" becomes "a3b1", "abc" becomes "a1b1c1"). Returns the encoded `str` with no side effects on the graph; the entry block prints the encoding of four sample strings.

Computes cumulative sums of an integer list. `running_total` takes `nums` (`list`) and returns a new `list` whose i-th element is the sum of the first i+1 inputs: a running sum `s` starts at 0, each value `v` is added in order, and the updated total is appended to `out` after every addition. The input list is left unmodified and an empty input yields an empty result; no side effects on the graph. The entry block prints the cumulative totals of five sample lists.

Returns the sign of an integer. `sign` takes `n` (`int`) and returns an `int`: 1 when `n` is positive, -1 when negative, and 0 when `n` is zero, using a simple comparison chain. Pure function with no side effects on the graph; the entry block prints the sign of five sample values covering all three cases.

Converts a phrase to snake case. `to_snake_case` lowercases `s` and replaces every space character with an underscore, returning the resulting `str` (e.g. "Hello World" becomes "hello_world"). Only literal spaces are translated -- other whitespace and punctuation pass through untouched, and consecutive spaces each become their own underscore. No side effects on the graph; the entry block prints three sample conversions.
